articles.title: Africa's richest man launches continent's biggest share sale
articles.summary: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote says he wants ordinary people to share in the success of his oil refinery.

blocks.text: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote has launched Africa's largest ever share sale, offering a stake in his oil refinery to the general public in a deal that could raise as much as $2.1bn (£1.6bn).
The initial public offering (IPO) is for roughly 3% of the Dangote refinery, with the billionaire saying he wanted to give ordinary Nigerians the chance to share in the plant's success.
The refinery, which started production in 2024, is one of the largest in the world and took more than a decade to complete.
It now supplies more than 70% of Nigeria's energy consumption, and many Nigerians have expressed excitement at the prospect of owning a part of it.
Among them is Isah Salisu, who told the BBC he withdrew 50,000 naira (£28; $37) from his savings to invest.
"My hope is that my small money will one day grow big. I don't want to miss out as many I know are also investing," he said.
The IPO lasts for a month and the minimum purchase is 10 shares, costing about $4.
Economy and business expert Dr Abdulrazak Ibrahim Fagge told the BBC that Monday's event was historic.
But he warned investors that the price of the shares could fall, meaning people could lose some of their money.
"What prospective buyers, especially first-time buyers, should know is that they shouldn't invest all their money or money they would need in a couple of months," he said.
"They should invest something they could do without for the next three, four, five years."
He also warned people to be wary of scammers, saying there are people who would want to take advantage of those without good knowledge of the process.
"I will advise people to only deal with the institutions that have been listed," he said.
Nigeria is Africa's biggest oil producer but until the refinery was opened, most of the country's fuel had to be imported because of a lack of refining capacity in the country.
Born in Kano, Dangote, 67, has a net worth of around $28bn, according to Forbes magazine.
He made his fortune in cement and sugar in Nigeria before expanding to 16 other African countries.
His company Dangote Cement is Africa's largest cement producer.
The Lagos refinery was first announced in 2013 with an initial estimated cost of around $19bn, but construction did not begin until 2017. It was further delayed by the Covid-19 pandemic.
The site, in the Lekki Free Zone near Lagos, required massive land reclamation, with 65 million cubic metres of sand moved.
The refinery has a processing capacity of 650,000 barrels per day, making it the seventh-largest in the world.
The money raised by the share offer is intended to help double its capacity.

articles.title: Government moves to nationalise Speciality Steel UK to protect 1,300 jobs
articles.summary: Firm, once part of Sanjeev Gupta’s empire, fell into administration last year but has failed to find buyer

blocks.text: One of Britain’s steelworks is to come into public ownership after the government said it would take over Yorkshire-based Speciality Steel UK (SSUK).

Jonathan Reynolds, the business secretary, said officials would “work towards” acquiring the company to protect the jobs of its 1,300 workers in Rotherham, Stocksbridge and Brinsworth in South Yorkshire and Wednesbury in the West Midlands.

The insolvent steelmaker, formerly part of the tycoon Sanjeev Gupta’s industrial empire, fell into administration last year and its day-to-day operations have since been run by the government’s official receiver.
The Norwegian steel startup Blastr Green Steel had been in talks to buy SSUK, but hopes had faded over the summer for a private sector takeover after a deadline to finalise a deal passed in June.
The steelworks and its staff have been described by Reynolds as important strategic assets for the UK. SSUK is the largest producer of “green steel”, made using less-polluting electric arc furnaces.
Reynolds said: “We do not intervene in private companies lightly. But nor can we simply stand aside and allow the future of this company and over 1,300 jobs to be decided by default.

“Working towards public acquisition will keep options open while we work with local leaders, workers, industry and investors to determine the best long-term future for these sites, which could play a vital role in the future of the growth-driving sectors in our industrial strategy, including defence and advanced manufacturing.

SSUK went bust last year after longstanding financial issues under previous ownership, particularly after the collapse of its primary lender Greensill Capital in 2021. A high court judge at the time found the company was “hopelessly insolvent”, with only £650,000 in the bank after running down its reserves.

Since then, the government has been funding the wages of its workers, costing £3.5m a month. The plants have not been producing steel for the last year, though some staff remain on its sites to maintain equipment.

Ministers’ preference was for a private sector buyer, but after what were described as “extensive discussions” with Blastr, officials decided the company’s offer could not provide the desired long-term stability for SSUK.
Mark Bula, the Blastr chief executive, quit the company unexpectedly at the end of last month, with its finance boss, David Morant, taking his place.
after newsletter promotion

The shadow business minister Bradley Thomas said it was “surprising” that the government had moved away from a private sector buyer after picking a preferred bidder. Speaking in parliament, he asked Reynolds: “Other than a new prime minister who’s committed ideologically to nationalisation, what has changed

Reynolds added there was “nothing ideological” about the move and that he would “not go into the detail” about why Blastr’s bid fell through. He accused the Conservatives of a “legacy of neglect” during their 14 years in government.

The government has committed to spending up to £2.5bn on the steel industry through the national wealth fund. About £500m of that was put towards converting Tata Steel’s blast furnaces into electric arc furnaces.

The South Yorkshire mayor, Oliver Coppard, said he was pleased the government had taken action, adding: “It’s the next important step forward, giving us more time to find the best possible outcome for our steelmaking communities – places where people have faced economic challenges and real barriers to opportunity for far too long.”

articles.title: UK armed forces member killed in crash in Ukraine
articles.summary:
Ministry of Defence says person died in road incident understood not to be result of hostile action

A member of the UK armed forces has been killed in a crash in Ukraine, the Ministry of…

blocks.text: A member of the UK armed forces has been killed in a crash in Ukraine, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) said.
The MoD said the person died in a road traffic incident on Saturday.
It is understood the incident was not as a result of hostile action.
Their family has been informed and has asked for some time before more details are released.
“Our thoughts and our sympathies are with the individual’s loved ones at this difficult time,” an MoD spokesperson said.
The defence secretary, Wes Streeting, said on X: “This is very sad news for the family and for those grieving with them in our Armed Forces.
“My deepest condolences go to them all.”
There is a small number of British personnel in Ukraine who provide security to diplomats and support the country’s armed forces.
British paratrooper George Hooley, 28, was killed in Ukraine in December when he watched Ukrainian forces testing a new defensive capability.
The MoD described his death as a “tragic accident”.
Russia’s full scale invasion of Ukraine is in its fifth year and the conflict continues with fresh strikes on Ukraine including at a gas works and a drone attack on a station on Sunday.
The attack hit a train at Yahodyn station, on the Polish border, shortly after a train carrying Boris Johnson had left ahead of schedule.
Ukraine’s railway operator said the attack may have been aimed at the train carrying the former prime minister, among other dignitaries.
Johnson had been returning from a major conference in Kyiv along with former Swedish prime minister Carl Bildt and a number of European security advisers.
According to a translation from Ukrainian, rail operator Ukrzaliznytsia said in a post on Telegram it was “quite possible” the drone had been aimed at Johnson’s train.

articles.title: Murad’s son beats ex-MILF commander for SGA 1st District seat in BARMM polls
articles.summary: The United Bangsamoro Justice Party’s Mansor Ebrahim is the son of Moro Islamic Liberation Front chairman Murad, who leads the central committee that axed the Bangsamoro Federalist Party’s Butch…

blocks.text: UBJP BET. Mansor Ebrahim of the United Bangsamoro Justice Party.
Ebrahim's Facebook page

The United Bangsamoro Justice Party’s Mansor Ebrahim is the son of Moro Islamic Liberation Front chairman Murad, who leads the central committee that axed the Bangsamoro Federalist Party’s Butch Malang as MILF commander

items: Mansor Ebrahim of the United Bangsamoro Justice Party won the 1st District seat in the Special Geographic Area, defeating Butch Malang of the Bangsamoro Federalist Party.
Ebrahim's victory allows him to serve a special five-year transition term in the Bangsamoro Parliament.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – The highly contested head-to-head race between the son of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) chairman and the high-ranking officer stripped of a position has finally concluded.

In the end, it was the MILF’s United Bangsamoro Justice Party that prevailed. The UBJP’s Mansor Ebrahim, the son of MILF Chairman Ahod “Al Haj Murad” Ebrahim, topped the race for the 1st District seat of the Special Geographic Area (SGA).
He received 29,061 votes, according to 100% of the SGA’s election returns for the 2026 Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao parliamentary elections as of Monday, September 14, 11:29 pm.

The Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP), the UBJP’s rival, fielded Butch Malang, who is the former SGA Development Authority administrator, a member of the region’s interim parliament, and the recently axed chair of the MILF Coordinating Committee on the Cessation of Hostilities.
Malang only got 17,386 votes.
The stakes were particularly high in this race because of Malang’s history with the MILF.

Just a week before the election, it was the central committee led by the Ebrahim patriarch that stripped Malang of his committee chairmanship. A news release by the MILF’s information committee owed it to “a leadership rift years in the making.”

It apparently began when President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. unceremoniously replaced the elder Ebrahim as interim chief minister with then-MILF army chief Abdulraof Macacua in March 2025. (READ: MILF central committee frowns on BARMM leadership change)

Tensions only grew as Macacua began making decisions as chief minister without consulting the MILF. In the end, Macacua and several other high-ranking MILF officials, including Malang, defected from the UBJP to the BFP.

Macacua, Malang, and their cohorts had been suspended from their positions in the Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces for months before they were eventually removed — though they remain members of the MILF.

With Malang defeated, the younger Ebrahim is set to serve a special five-year transition term from October 30, 2026, to June 30, 2031. He will be one of the 32 district representatives making up 40% of the 80-seat Bangsamoro Parliament. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Defense questions ex-Sandigan presiding justice as witness
articles.summary: The defense panel has questioned the decision of the prosecution to present retired Sandiganbayan presiding justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang as the Senate impeachment court tackles the article on the…

blocks.text: September 15, 2026 | 12:00am
Retired Sandiganbayan presiding justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang appears before the Senate impeachment court on September 14, 2026.
SPPA

MANILA, Philippines — The defense panel has questioned the decision of the prosecution to present retired Sandiganbayan presiding justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang as the Senate impeachment court tackles the article on the alleged unexplained wealth of Vice President Sara Duterte.
In a manifestation, defense lawyer Mark Vinluan said the presentation of Cabotaje-Tang is improper.

“This is the first time that the Vice President is being confronted with Justice Tang and her testimony. For the record, she is not listed in the pre-trial order as a witness and there is no reservation for a witness with her designation or background,” said Vinluan.
“So, for all intents and purposes, Justice Tang is a surprise witness, which violates fair play and is prohibited under the rules,” Vinluan said.
“In light of the foregoing, we will move for the exclusion of the testimony of Justice Tang and will submit to this Court’s discretion as to the presentation of her testimony,” Vinluan said.

He added that the prosecution did not even furnish the defense with copies beforehand, saying that this is already the third time that the prosecution has attempted to present a witness without first furnishing the defense with the materials to be used.
“We don’t know her personal background, and we don’t know the extent of her testimony and the documents that she will identify, if any,” Vinluan noted.
According to Vinluan, the notice on Sept. 9 was only to Cabotaje-Tang’s name, previous official function and general purpose of her testimony.
He said it is the position of the defense that the presentation of Cabotaje-Tang infringes on the Vice President’s right to intelligently cross-examine her.

“And more importantly, (it) violates the Vice President’s constitutional right to due process, particularly her right to be promptly and completely informed of the nature and cause of the accusation against her,” he added.
Vinluan noted that in the Philippines, being a legal expert is not an official designation and is quite subjective.
“We don’t know the extent of her legal knowledge, her political background, whether she’s neutral, DDS, loyalista or kakampink, which is hardly distinguishable nowadays,” he noted.
Presumption of innocence
The defense maintained that the Vice President enjoys presumption of innocence as the prosecution is “hellbent” on removing her from office.
During cross-examination of Cabotaje-Tang, Vinluan stressed that it is not the prosecution’s primary duty to convict.
“The prosecution should not be too eager to convict. Vice President Sara enjoys the presumption of innocence, correct?” Vinluan said.
He said that if the prosecution fails “to discharge this burden,” Duterte is entitled to an acquittal.
“At any rate, conviction must be based on the strength of the prosecution and not the weakness of the defense,” Vinluan added.
Cabotaje-Tang agreed with Vinluan but based on the point of view of criminal lawyers.
Oral arguments
The defense is ready for the oral arguments on the two-thirds threshold to convict the Vice President.
Defense spokesman Michael Poa said they have decided who will represent Duterte during the oral arguments but will not disclose the name.

Impeachment court spokesman Reginald Tongol said the Senate impeachment court will need 11 votes from the active roster of 20 senators to overturn the ruling setting the conviction threshold at 16 votes in Duterte’s impeachment trial. — Marc Jayson Cayabyab

articles.title: 64% say district reps ‘doing a good job’ – OCTA
articles.summary: About six in every 10 Filipinos believe that their district representatives are doing a good job, indicating what the OCTA Research group described as a stark difference between views at the local…

blocks.text: September 15, 2026 | 12:00am
President Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr. delivered his fifth State of the Nation Address at plenary hall of the House of Representatives in Quezon City, July 27, 2026.
Philippine STAR / Noel B. Pabalate

MANILA, Philippines — About six in every 10 Filipinos believe that their district representatives are doing a good job, indicating what the OCTA Research group described as a stark difference between views at the local and institutional levels.
In its July 4 to 11 survey, OCTA found 64 percent of the respondents agreed their current district representatives were doing a good job. Only 27 percent disagreed, while nine percent were undecided.
This is far higher than the 38 percent trust and 37 percent performance rating obtained by the House of Representatives as an institution.

“The finding that local representative satisfaction substantially exceeds institutional trust and institutional performance ratings suggests that accountability in Philippine politics may operate more effectively, or at least more visibly, at the constituency level than at the level of the institution itself,” OCTA said.

“This has implications beyond public opinion measurement: it bears on how legislators themselves may calculate political incentives, since a representative’s standing with constituents appears largely decoupled from the public’s broader assessment of Congress,” it added.

The survey firm said it may also offer partial explanation for a familiar pattern in Philippine electoral behavior showing high incumbent reelection rates despite low institutional trust in Congress as a whole.
OCTA pointed out how regional variation in satisfaction with district representation “is not a uniform national mood, but a locally contingent one.”

articles.title: Economy ‘more than steady’ – Marcos
articles.summary: Despite inflation concerns and the weakening of the peso, President Marcos described the Philippines as “more than steady.”

blocks.text: September 15, 2026 | 12:00am
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at Malacañang on February 23, 2026.
PPA pool photos by Niño Jesus Orbeta
MANILA, Philippines — Despite inflation concerns and the weakening of the peso, President Marcos described the Philippines as “more than steady.”

Speaking to reporters in New Delhi on Sunday, Marcos attributed the weakness of the peso and higher unemployment partly to inflation and reduced public spending following the flood control corruption scandal.

“The peso to the dollar, it’s because of inflation, because of all the weaknesses that we are seeing. Unemployment went up. And that’s, again, because of lack of public spending. That’s the effect there. So at least it’s something that we can do something about and are doing something about,” Marcos said.

He declined to make promises about inflation, citing high oil prices and the continuing Middle East conflict, but said economic improvements should become visible as government spending increases and more jobs are created.
Inflation eased to 6.1 percent in August from 6.2 percent in July as food prices rose at a slower pace.
However, average inflation for the first eight months reached 5.2 percent, well above the government’s full-year target of three percent.

Unemployment also climbed to six percent in July from 4.9 percent in June and 5.3 percent a year earlier, translating to 3.14 million jobless Filipinos. It was the highest unemployment rate since June 2022, according to the Philippine Statistics Authority.

To address this, the President said the administration was expanding assistance programs to cushion vulnerable sectors from the impact of the Middle East crisis, including subsidies for farmers and scholarships.

“The UPLIFT program is having a good effect, we see in the stats that those that are being reached by these programs are widening in terms of who gets assistance from the government as the... systems of assistance become more established,” he said.
National government outstanding debt reached P19.39 trillion at the end of July.

Marcos made the remarks before returning to Manila early Monday after a two-day working visit to New Delhi, where he represented the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations at the 18th BRICS Summit. — Helen Flores

articles.title: Manibela hits ‘deals’ to delay strike
articles.summary: Some transport leaders were offered “personal deals” to discourage them from joining the strike, transport group Manibela said yesterday.

blocks.text: September 15, 2026 | 12:00am
Members of transport group Manibela stage a protest at Philcoa in Quezon City yesterday, marking the first day of their planned two-day transport strike.
Michael Varcas
MANILA, Philippines — Some transport leaders were offered “personal deals” to discourage them from joining the strike, transport group Manibela said yesterday.

Officials of the Department of Transportation (DOTr) and Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) asked leaders to defer participation in exchange for granting their requests, Manibela chairman Mar Valbuena said.
Declining to name officials and transport leaders, Valbuena said they are “catering to the demands of the leaders so that they alone can benefit.”
“In the coming days, we will not announce the transport strike’s schedule so other transport groups being courted by the DOTr and LTFRB will not be dragged into it,” he added.
Manibela is staging a two-day strike as pump prices are expected to rise this week, with diesel prices projected to increase by P2 to P2.50 per liter and gasoline by P4.50 to P5 per liter.

Valbuena stressed that the protest aims to urge the government to implement a fare hike of P2 as public utility vehicles (PUVs) will shoulder almost P100 per liter of petroleum. — Bella Cariaso, EJ Macababbad

articles.title: 2 areas in BARMM placed under Comelec control
articles.summary: Two areas in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao were placed under the control of the Commission on Elections following reports of violent incidents and compromised ballots during the…

blocks.text: September 15, 2026 | 12:00am
The Bangsamoro regional capitol in Cotabato City.
Philstar.com / John Unson

MANILA, Philippines — Two areas in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) were placed under the control of the Commission on Elections (Comelec) following reports of violent incidents and compromised ballots during the region’s first parliamentary elections.

“The Comelec en banc has decided to place Cotabato City under Comelec control and that we are set to designate an administrator that will supervise the elections in the city. This is due to the shooting incident last night as well as the use of an explosive device that hurt the perpetrator himself who is now in a hospital,” Comelec Chairman George Garcia said.
He added that a heated argument among voters lining up at a precinct as early as 11 p.m. Sunday night led to fisticuffs and later shootings.
The municipality of Maluso in Basilan was also placed under Comelec control following the discovery of pre-shaded ballots in the town’s 36 precincts.

“We learned that these ballots were pre-shaded so we placed it under Comelec control. We assigned a Comelec official, a member of the special action team who is in Basilan right now as the administrator,” Garcia said.
The poll body chief said they immediately ordered the reprinting of ballots.
In a separate interview with “Storycon” on One News, Garcia said they expect most of the winners to be proclaimed before noon today.
“We are really happy. Throughout the day… despite the challenges and incidents we encountered, our fellow Filipinos were able to cast their votes,” he said.

In a video statement, President Marcos described the first BARMM parliamentary elections as a “defining moment” in the history of the region. — Janvic Mateo, Rainier Allan Ronda, Alexis Romero, Mark Ernest Villeza, Evelyn Macairan, Gerry Lee Gorit, Bella Cariaso, Delon Porcalla, Roel Pareño

articles.title: BIR scraps VAT on system loss charge
articles.summary: The Bureau of Internal Revenue has formally removed the value-added tax on the allowable system loss charge in electricity bills, a move seen to lower the amount passed on to consumers.

blocks.text: September 15, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) has formally removed the value-added tax (VAT) on the allowable system loss charge in electricity bills, a move seen to lower the amount passed on to consumers.

In its Revenue Memorandum Circular (RMC) 97-2026, the BIR recognizes the allowable system loss charge within the cap approved by the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) as a government-mandated charge excluded from gross sales for VAT purposes.
The BIR said the exclusion will apply prospectively in accordance with the effectivity of ERC Resolution 26, Series of 2026.

“For consumers, the practical effect is straightforward: once the new rules become effective, VAT will no longer be imposed on the allowable system loss portion of the electricity bill. That means a lower amount will be passed on to consumers on covered billings and transactions,” BIR Commissioner Charlito Martin Mendoza said.
The Philippines has the most expensive electricity rates among its Southeast Asian neighbors, according to the Department of Energy.
The circular said the charge will not be subject to output VAT and creditable withholding on VAT.
The exclusion, however, does not extend to income tax and the corresponding creditable withholding tax.
For VAT purposes, the BIR said allowable system loss charge must be separately identified in the billing statement, invoice or similar document.

Generation companies, the National Grid Corp. of the Philippines, distribution utilities, electric cooperatives and other affected taxpayers must also ensure proper billing, accounting, reporting and separate identification of the charge in accordance with applicable ERC rules and tax regulations.
Mendoza said that while the issuance may be just a fraction of a broader push to bring down electricity costs, it provides relief that can be implemented under existing law.
“While Congress continues to consider wider reforms on electricity charges and taxes, the BIR is acting on the measures within its authority that can reduce the burden on consumers,” Mendoza said.

The issuance builds on the BIR’s earlier action on government-mandated electricity charges. Under RMC 60-2026, the agency had clarified the tax treatment of the Lifeline Subsidy, Green Energy Auction Allowance and other specified government-mandated charges.
Fuel price hikes

Meanwhile, gasoline, diesel and kerosene prices are set to climb by as much as P5.68, P4.31 and P4.62 per liter, respectively, today, according to the Department of Energy, as the regional benchmark Dubai crude surged past $100 a barrel to hit $116 last week.
For the 30-day period ending Sept. 11, the average Dubai crude price stood at $99.41 per barrel, DOE-Oil Industry Management Bureau director Rino Abad said.
Energy Secretary Sharon Garin said the DOE had already informed the Department of Finance of the breaching of the Dubai crude price threshold.
“So that’s for them to decide whether to do suspension – total or no suspension, or partial suspension,” Garin said in a chance interview yesterday, referring to fuel excise tax.
Under Republic Act 12316, the President may suspend or reduce fuel excise taxes when the average price of Dubai crude exceeds $80 per barrel for a month.
‘Suspend excise tax on diesel, gas’
Also on excise tax, Regasco is urging the DOE to recommend suspending the one imposed on diesel and gasoline and not just on liquefied petroleum gas or LPG.
Regasco president Arnel Ty said he had already written Garin about his proposal.
In an interview with radio dzMM, Ty said suspending excise taxes on three widely used energy products will provide much-needed relief for consumers.

“In our opinion and assessment, the problem is more serious now because we are going into the ‘ber months,’” Ty said. “And it looks like Iran and the United States are becoming more stubborn because there’s an upcoming election in November in America.”
A suspension of excise taxes would mean a P10 per liter cut on gasoline prices and P6 on diesel, while LPG prices would fall by P3 per kilogram. — Brix Lelis, EJ Macababbad

articles.title: FLP to honor law scholars, MBA fellows, dissertation writing winners
articles.summary: The Foundation for Liberty & Prosperity will celebrate the newest recipients of its academic awards on Sept. 16 at the Manila Polo Club, with First Lady Liza Marcos as special guest and Bangko…

blocks.text: September 15, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Foundation for Liberty & Prosperity (FLP) will celebrate the newest recipients of its academic awards on Sept. 16 at the Manila Polo Club, with First Lady Liza Marcos as special guest and Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Governor Eli Remolona Jr. as guest speaker.

The ceremony will bring together awardees from three FLP education programs – 20 law scholars who will each receive P250,000; five Master of Business Administration fellows in entrepreneurship, sustainability, management, economics and business law (ESMEL) who will each receive P500,000, and the 11 winners and finalists of the Dissertation Writing Contest, with prizes totaling P1.3 million.

Awardees will be presented with certificates, plaques, cash grants and other prizes by the First Lady, retired chief justice Artemio Panganiban as FLP chairman and the heads of the respective boards of judges.

The annual recognition program reflects FLP’s commitment to supporting students who combine academic distinction with a demonstrated commitment to the foundation’s ideals and who show promise in carrying those principles into their chosen professions.
Law scholars

In partnership with the Tan Yan Kee Foundation, FLP will extend P250,000 scholarships to 10 fourth year law students and 10 third-year law students. The third year scholars are Franz Arcamo (USC), Krislen Bismonte (UST), Kevin Francisco (FEU), Lourdes Galeon (USC), Angel Letrondo (USC), Rafael Maliwanag (UP), Robert Marcos (University of Southeastern Philippines), Beatrice Puente (UP), Maroel San Pedro (UP) and Justine Sarsuelo (DLSU).

The fourth-year law scholars will receive the same P250,000 grants. They are Althea Acidre (Dr. V. Orestes Romualdez Educational Foundation), Dannielle Caliosan (University of Southeastern Philippines), Jan Davocol (ADMU), Kim Humarang (UST), Alyannah Mabelin (UC), Lia Manalo (UP), Joselino Poquiz (ADMU), Myka Reambonanza (USC), Brian Unabia (USC) and Michelle Vergara (USC).
Three scholars who took last year’s Bar examinations placed among the top 20: Enrico Paguia of ADMU ranked 6th, Ignacio Villareal of UP, 15th and Chinzen Viernes of UP, 19th.

The law scholars were selected by a board chaired by Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo, with Solicitor General Darlene Marie Berberabe, dean Jose Grapilon, Evelyn Abao and FLP corporate secretary Joel Gregorio as members.
Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo, board of judges, SC Justice Henri Jean Paul Inting, board of judges and Former BSP governor Amando Tetangco Jr., board of judges
MBA fellows

In partnership with Metro Pacific Investments Corp. through the Metro Pacific Investments Foundation, FLP will award P500,000 fellowship grants to Cindy Alteros (AIM), Mary Beltran (AIM), Ingrid Lazo (ADMU), Amity Lim (ADMU) and Stephanie Suarez (UP).
The ESMEL fellows were chosen by a board led by former BSP governor Amando Tetangco Jr., together with Chaye Cabal-Revilla, Monette Iturralde Hamlin, Marilen Yaptangco and Joel Gregorio.
Dissertation writing contest winners

FLP, in partnership with Ayala Corp., will also recognize the awardees of its Dissertation Writing program. Roberto Bedonia (UP Iloilo Extension) will receive the P320,000 first prize, while Therese Germinanda (West Visayas State University) will receive the P220,000 second prize.
The third place awardees, each to receive P120,000, are Joshua Tambor (UV), Edeleine Reyes (De La Salle Lipa) and Mel Castro (USC). The five winning dissertations are available at www.libpros.com.

Finalist awards of P20,000 each will be given to Aaron Lagmay (FEU), Charmaine Candaroma (San Sebastian College-Recoletos), Diadem Lanayon (FEU), Charles Rey (ADMU), Hannah Carmona (FEU) and Joerome Rimorin (FEU).

The dissertation winners were evaluated by a board headed by SC Justice Henri Jean Paul Inting, with Court of Tax Appeals Justice Ivy Reyes-Fajardo, Ayala Corp. chief legal officer Franchette Acosta, dean Anna Maria Abad and Joel Gregorio.

articles.title: Ex-justice: VP may be removed for hiding assets
articles.summary: Impeachable officials like Vice President Sara Duterte may be removed from office for “intentional concealment” of assets including those owned by their spouses, according to retired…

blocks.text: September 15, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Impeachable officials like Vice President Sara Duterte may be removed from office for “intentional concealment” of assets including those owned by their spouses, according to retired Sandiganbayan presiding justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang.

The issue of Duterte’s alleged ill-gotten wealth took center stage on Day 24 of the impeachment trial, focusing on the Vice President’s joint bank accounts with her husband, lawyer Maneses Carpio, and her alleged failure to divest her businesses while in office.

When Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian in his interjection asked the witness about the disparity between an official’s declared wealth in their statement of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN) and an unexplained “wealth accumulation,” Cabotaje-Tang said it is “unacceptable,” especially if there is a repeat offense in misdeclaring their net worth. Cabotaje-Tang agreed with Gatchalian’s question that “unexplained wealth” is a “ground for removal or dismissal” under the anti-graft law Republic Act 3019.

About declaring assets with their spouses, Cabotaje-Tang said a recent Supreme Court decision has a “qualification” that a married couple can come up with an “agreement of a complete separation of property before their marriage” that may exempt the public official from declaring their joint assets.
Without that agreement, a public official has to declare these joint assets, including businesses, properties and cash, or else he or she would be “penalized,” Cabotaje-Tang said.
“It’s only the government official, sir, who is required to file a SALN. And that public official is required to include the assets of his or her spouse,” she said.

An official may not be charged with “intentional concealment” if the public official was kept in the dark about joint bank accounts with their spouse, Cabotaje-Tang said, citing another Supreme Court case.
Gatchalian asked Cabotaje-Tang if a public official with no intention of truthfully declaring their joint assets may be removed from office.
“Yes, sir,” Cabotaje-Tang said.
Officials must divest
Duterte’s lawyers vehemently tried but failed to block the testimony of Cabotaje-Tang, who underwent direct examination by Rep. Chel Diokno of party-list Akbayan.

When asked about her opinion on high officials like the president, vice president and Cabinet members on the provision of “conflict of interest,” Cabotaje-Tang maintained that all of them should “divest” any and all kinds of business interests, even a sari-sari store.

Cabotaje-Tang said the rationale is that their high positions in government might tempt them to abuse the industry they are representing, as they wield discretionary powers that could repeatedly result in decisions that would favor them.
This may happen – directly or indirectly – in firms which the government officials themselves manage while in office.

“It has been very clear in her testimony that the President and VP are barred from involving themselves in any business enterprise, that is as clear as sunlight,” House prosecution adviser and spokesman Robert Ace Barbers stressed during a press conference.

The prosecution made the assertion after Cabotaje-Tang discussed the distinction between retaining legitimate investments and continuing to participate in business while occupying the presidency or vice presidency.

For her part, House prosecutor and San Juan Rep. Bel Zamora explained that the business issue forms one of three separate components prosecutors intend to establish under Article II of the impeachment complaint against Duterte.

“The first one is amassing unexplained wealth. The second is the SALN violation. And the third is the failure to declare or divest business interests. So, these are three aspects of the unexplained wealth article,” she said.
Abuse of power
Cabotaje-Tang explained that the Constitution imposes an absolute ban on the president and vice president from participating in any business to prevent abuse of power.
Presiding officer Sen. Francis Escudero asked if the ban simply means the top officials cannot actively manage a company or if they are totally barred from owning one, even a sari-sari store.
Cabotaje-Tang said the prohibition covers both direct and indirect participation, including mere ownership or serving as a corporate director.
She emphasized that the president and vice president are legally required to divest from all business interests within 30 days of assuming office.
She clarified that the government’s pursuit of unexplained wealth has no expiration date.

Sen. Erwin Tulfo asked if there is a time limit for the state to investigate an official’s wealth, citing hypothetical scenarios where an incumbent mayor’s assets from their time as a barangay councilor 15 years prior are suddenly scrutinized.
“Under the Constitution, the right of the state to recover unlawfully acquired wealth is imprescriptible,” she told Tulfo.
During her testimony, she and Escudero discussed a technical loophole in how public officials declare their wealth through the SALN.
Escudero pointed out that the SALN captures a snapshot of an official’s wealth specifically as of Dec. 31 of the previous year.
He asked Cabotaje-Tang if a massive amount of money that enters an official’s bank account in October and is withdrawn by November should be declared in the April 30 filing.
She conceded that such funds would legally escape the declaration. — Neil Jayson Servallos, EJ Macababbad

articles.title: Senate OKs 5-year barangay, SK term bill
articles.summary: The Senate yesterday passed on third and final reading a bill seeking to fix the terms of barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan officials at five years, effectively postponing the upcoming Nov. 2…

blocks.text: September 15, 2026 | 12:00am
Thirteen senators voted for the measure pushed by Sen. Francis Escudero while five opposed it.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate yesterday passed on third and final reading a bill seeking to fix the terms of barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan officials at five years, effectively postponing the upcoming Nov. 2 barangay and SK elections (BSKE).
Senators Francis Pangilinan and Bam Aquino opposed the measure, citing village residents’ right to suffrage and to run for office, particularly the youth.
“We need their boundless energy, courage and conscience in the barangays. We need fresh voices, new ideas and new blood in local leadership. As they say, ‘no cap,’” Pangilinan said.
“It is time to give the new generation of leaders a chance. That is why my decision is clear that the BSKE should proceed this November, and hence, I vote ‘no,’” Aquino said.
Also voting against the bill were Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente Sotto III and Sens. Risa Hontiveros and Joel Villanueva.
Sotto said his turno en contra speech against postponing the BSKE served as his explanation for voting “No.”

In his speech last Wednesday, when the bill was approved on second reading, Sotto said the five-year BSK term could be fixed without another postponement of the elections, which he noted would already be the eighth time.
Under the bill, the BSKE scheduled for Nov. 2 would be moved to the second Monday of November 2028 and every five years thereafter.
Incumbent elected barangay officials “shall be regarded as having completed one term... considering the extension of their terms by two years,” the bill states.
Those currently serving their third consecutive term would be considered ineligible to run for the same position in the proposed 2028 elections.

articles.title: Marcos on Sara tirades: You can’t force anyone to love you
articles.summary: Not even the most powerful man in the land can demand affection.

blocks.text: September 15, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — Not even the most powerful man in the land can demand affection.

President Marcos chose to be economical with his words in reacting to Vice President Sara Duterte’s string of tirades against him, including a demand for him to resign because of the alleged “abuses” of his administration.

“You know, I hear about them, but I don’t really even have a response,” Marcos told reporters at the close of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi on Sunday. “If she feels very angry, I suppose, with what’s happening to her, and I am the target of that anger, or the main target of that anger, what can I do? You cannot force anyone to love you.”

Marcos and Duterte were close political allies, running under the now defunct UniTeam coalition and winning by a landslide in the 2022 national elections. But their relationship has soured, a political divorce that became evident when Duterte resigned as education secretary and vice chairperson of the government’s anti-insurgency task force in June 2024. A series of political shockwaves, including Duterte’s impeachment and the arrest of her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte, over alleged crimes against humanity, further strained the Vice President’s ties with the Marcos administration. Duterte is undergoing impeachment trial for allegedly misuse of confidential funds, committing bribery, amassing unexplained wealth and issuing death threats against Marcos, First Lady Liza Marcos and former House speaker Martin Romualdez. Last Friday, the Quezon City Regional Trial Court issued an arrest warrant against Duterte over her grave threat charges but she posted a P360,000 bail the following day.
In remarks delivered before her supporters over the weekend, Duterte said she would continue to call for the resignation of Marcos, describing him as “shameless, corrupt, an addict.”
‘Salo-salo sa Palasyo’
President Marcos celebrated his birthday yesterday with a throng of supporters during a “Salo-salo sa Palasyo” at Malacañang.
Marcos, who turned 69 on Sunday, was in New Delhi over the weekend.
“You have made this a very, very, very happy birthday for me. Thank you very much. We love you very much,” Marcos said during the celebration at the Kalayaan Grounds.
Marcos was accompanied by the First Lady.
The guests were treated with magic shows and cultural performances.
Birthday wish
At a press conference in New Delhi, Marcos wished he could spend more time with his family, noting that their schedules often do not match.

“I suppose for my family, it’s simple. I wish I saw more of all of you. And it’s not just my children, including the First Lady. Our schedules don’t match very well. We don’t see each other that much either. I wish I could spend more time with all of you, number one,” the President said.
The Chief Executive also wished that the reforms he started would continue beyond his administration.
“We will continue to make it better,” he said.
Marcos happy with Imelda’s acquittal
President Marcos is happy that the Supreme Court has overturned the 2018 graft conviction of his mother, former first lady Imelda Marcos.

“I’m glad that that case is over. It’s been hanging over our heads for about 40 years. All those cases were filed in 1986, and that’s how long it’s taken,” Marcos said at a press conference in New Delhi on Sunday.
“I’m happy that, you know, she doesn’t have to be worried about it any longer, because she does worry about these cases. Yeah, I’m glad especially for my mother,” Marcos said.

In a 50-page ruling penned by Associate Justice Rodil Zalameda, the SC’s First Division overturned the conviction by the Sandiganbayan of the former first lady on seven counts of graft involving her alleged financial interests in private foundations in Switzerland.

In 2018, the anti-graft court found the former first lady, who turned 97 last July, guilty of seven counts of graft, sentencing her from six years and one month to 11 years of imprisonment for each count.

The cases stemmed from allegations that the President’s mother, while serving as governor of Metro Manila and holding other government positions during the administration of her late husband, former president Ferdinand Marcos Sr., maintained financial interests in several private foundations based in Switzerland.
The President, meanwhile, dismissed claims the high court’s decision could influence the selection of the next chief justice.
“No, no. That’s the first time I made any connection between the choice of Chief Justice and no, that’s never been, that will never enter our thinking in any way,” Marcos said.

The speculation came after three members of the SC First Division that decided the case have been considered among the frontrunners to succeed Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo. They are Associate Justices Jhosep Lopez, Henri Jean Paul Inting and Mario Lopez.

The SC found inadmissible as evidence the Swiss documents that were the main basis of the prosecution’s allegation that the former first lady had a financial and pecuniary interest in the foundations.

It said the Sandiganbayan erred in considering the documents as authenticated, as these did not satisfy provisions under Rule 132 of the Rules of Court in the authentication of private documents. — Helen Flores

articles.title: Martin Romualdez placed in QC Jail infirmary with PDLs under medical monitoring -BJMP
articles.summary: Former Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez has been placed in the infirmary of the Quezon City Jail in Payatas, the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology said on Monday night.

blocks.text: Published September 14, 2026 11:57pm
Former Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez has been placed in the infirmary of the Quezon City Jail in Payatas, the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology said on Monday night.
In a statement, the BJMP confirmed the commitment to the QC Jail male dormitory of the Leyte congressman, who is accused of plunder related to P7.2 billion in alleged kickbacks.

"Considering his medical needs and the medical recommendations presented before the Court, Rep. Romualdez has been placed in the jail infirmary together with other [persons deprived of liberty] requiring medical monitoring," the BJMP said.
The BJMP said the arrangement is in accordance with BJMP policies and the Sandiganbayan’s directives to ensure that his continuing medical needs are properly attended to.

"The BJMP assures the public that it will remain professional, impartial, and consistent in the implementation of its rules and regulations. All PDL under its custody are treated fairly and humanely, without distinction or privilege based on status or position," the BJMP said.
The Sandiganbayan on Monday ordered the commitment Romualdez to the male dormitory of the Quezon City Jail.
In its order dated September 14, the Third Division also set his arraignment on Wednesday, September 16.
This was after doctors told the court that Romualdez's condition didn't require confinement in a hospital.
The former Speaker had been in a hospital since his arrest; first the Cardinal Santos Medical Center, and then at the Philippine General Hospita.

"Accordingly, the court commits to the Quezon City Jail - Male Dormitory the living person of accused Romualdez, who is charged for the crime of plunder, to be held therein as a detention prisoner and as such, the accused shall not be moved, removed, transferred, and/or otherwise be released therefrom unless ordered by the court," the court said.
"The parties are reminded that the arraignment and pre-trial of this case as to accused Romualdez is set on Wednesday, September 16, 2026 at 8:30 in the morning," it added. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: Trump says he will consider releasing more 9/11 records after families’ request
articles.summary:
Families have asked Trump to declassify records that could shed light on Saudi Arabia’s alleged role in the 2001 attacks

Donald…

blocks.text: Donald Trump said Sunday that he will look into requests from families of 9/11 victims to release records that could shed light on Saudi Arabia’s alleged role in the attacks 25 years ago.

Several families have long alleged that a group of extremist religious leaders in Saudi Arabia gained influence in the kingdom’s government and aided the hijackers. Fifteen of the 19 hijackers were Saudis, but the Saudi government has long denied any involvement in the attacks.
The families have asked Trump to declassify and release the relevant records. Asked about it on Sunday during his trip to Ireland, the president said he would consider it.
“I’m going to look at it when I get back,” Trump said just before boarding Air Force One to return to Washington after a weekend in Ireland. “I know they asked me Friday.”

The relatives of 9/11 victims have been engaged in a lengthy legal battle against the Saudis. One of them, Terry Strada, called on Trump during a remembrance in New York City on Friday to “tell the Saudis to stop lying”.
Strada, who lost her husband, Tom, on 9/11, said US presidents had chosen “to protect the Saudis instead of standing with the 9/11 families”.

Strada, who was one of the 9/11 family members who read aloud the names of victims at the remembrance on the 25th anniversary of the attacks, added that the current administration should “stand with the families, stand with the survivors”.
“It has been one betrayal after another,” she said. “President Trump can still change that.”

articles.title: Macklemore dropped from Ed Sheeran’s US tour after ‘free Palestine’ speech
articles.summary:
The American rapper will no longer support Sheeran’s US leg of Loop tour after comments at MetLife Stadium show

Macklemore has been…

blocks.text: Macklemore has been dropped from the remainder of the US leg of Ed Sheeran’s Loop tour, after the American rapper drew headlines for saying “free Palestine” on stage at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

In a brief speech between songs on 4 September, the Grammy-winning artist told the audience he wanted the people of Gaza and “the occupied West Bank” to know “we have not forgotten about them”, prompting a petition from the Israeli American Council demanding his removal from the tour.

Messina Touring Group, the promoter of the US leg of Sheeran’s tour, told Rolling Stone: “As the concert promoter for Ed Sheeran’s US Loop Tour, we have been notified by venues on the upcoming US tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans. After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will not be performing on the remaining support dates.” Macklemore and Sheeran did not immediately reply to requests for comment.

The Seattle-bred rapper was slated to open for Sheeran at eight of the remaining 10 shows of his US Loop tour, which will resume on 19 September in Philadelphia. The venues that allegedly objected to Macklemore’s return include stadiums in that city as well as outside Boston, Atlanta, Charlotte, Indianapolis, Dallas and Tampa.

Macklemore, long an outspoken supporter of the rights for Palestinians and those in Gaza, delivered the remarks at his first appearance on the Loop tour on 4 September. “A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: ‘Free Palestine,’” he said in a two-minute speech. “I said: ‘Free Palestine!’ I want those words to be loud and clear, so that people all the way in Gaza to the occupied West Bank know that we have not forgotten about them.”

Alluding to possible controversy, he added that not “speaking my heart in order to keep my own comfort, and the audience’s comfort … is the day that I no longer deserve to be on stage”, and called US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) a “terrorist organization”. He also showed images of the devastation from Israeli military attacks in Gaza during his protest anthem Hind’s Hall, which celebrated protesters’ occupation of a building they named in honor of Hind Rajab, a six-year-old killed by the Israeli military in 2024.

The comments spurred the group StopAntisemitism to accuse the musician of “ambushing fans” with “anti-Israel propaganda” in an Instagram post that was amplified by the singer Pink. In another post, Pink explained that she did not object to Macklemore saying “free Palestine” but added: “I have never asked for another artist to be silenced and I’m not asking now. I don’t need anyone fired, and I don’t need a refund. What I need is to be able to say, as a Jewish mom, ‘that scared me, and it scared people I love,’ without being told our fear is just propaganda, and without being told I’m somehow cool with genocide because I noticed?”

The Israeli American Council also called for Macklemore to be removed from the tour, claiming his statements raised the question of “where the line should be drawn when an opening act uses a global concert platform to advance a one-sided political agenda”.

At the second of his appearances at MetLife on 5 September, Macklemore reiterated his support for Palestine and addressed Jewish members of the audience: “Criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide in no way is a criticism of you. My message is for peace, love; for all human beings to be treated with dignity, respect and equality.”

The North American leg of Sheeran’s tour will conclude in November at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida, which earlier this year hosted two shows by Ye, the rapper formerly known as Kanye West, who has a history of antisemitic statements. Tour openers Lukas Graham and Aaron Rowe are set to take the stage as planned.

articles.title: Yemen's Houthis attack Saudis, seize crucial Red Sea islands
articles.summary: Iran-backed Houthi rebels have tightened their grip on a key shipping route, capturing two strategic Red Sea islands. The closure of another global transport route is the latest ripple effect of the…

image.caption: With the Strait of Hormuz already closed, Houthi control of the Bab al-Mandab passage only increases pressure on Saudi Arabia and the USImage: Osamah Abdulrahman/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Iranian-backed Houthi rebels on Monday announced they had captured Greater and Lesser Hanish Island in the southern Red Sea.
The move bolsters the group's ability to choke traffic in another key global maritime shipping route as the ripple-effect of the war in Iran grows.

The strategic advance comes as Saudi-backed Yemeni forces try to regain territory recently lost near the Bab el-Mandab Strait, an important alternative to the Strait of Hormuz — which Iran has held closed since US President Donald Trump began bombing the Islamic Republic on February 28.

The closure of the Hormuz Strait, through which roughly one-fifth of the world's oil passed before the US began hostilities, has led to a global economic and energy emergency, driving up prices around the world and forcing petro-monarchy Saudi Arabia to move its oil exports through Bab el-Mandab.
But the Houthis have declared a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia and last week seized strategic Mayun Island and the Red Sea port of Mokha, cutting off the alternative route.
The capture of Greater and Lesser Hanish now puts even more pressure on Saudi shipments and thus global oil supplies and prices.

Beyond putting the squeeze on Saudi Arabia — the Houthis' proxy enemy for backing the internationally recognized government in the Yemen's reignited civil war — it could also provide Iran added leverage in defending itself against the US.
Houthis seize Red Sea chokepoint: What can Saudi Arabia do?
Houthi offensive continues to escalate as Iran war expands
The Houthis pressed on with their offensive Monday, launching missile and drone attacks on Saudi military targets.
A spokesman for the group said the strikes had caused "significant damage" and had come in response to "more than 300 [Saudi] airstrikes in [Yemen over] the past five days."
Despite being a longtime backer of the Houthis as part of its anti-Israel "axis of resistance," Tehran has denied any involvement in Yemen's revived civil war.

"Iran does not interfere in Yemeni affairs," said Tehran's Foreign Ministry on Monday, with spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei telling reporters the Houthis are "entirely independent actors who make their decisions based on their own interests."

Yemen's civil war — dormant for four years until the conflict in Iran broke out — began in 2014, when Houthi rebels seized large parts of northern Yemen, including the capital Sanaa, and forced the government to flee to Aden in the south.
In 2015, Saudi Arabia led a military coalition aiding the government, launching wave after wave of airstrikes as the conflict escalated into one of the worst humanitarian disasters in the world.
Saudi oil pipeline attack could raise global gas prices
Concerning situation for US and its Saudi, Gulf State allies
On Monday, Admiral Brad Cooper of US Central Command (CENTCOM) was in Jeddah to discuss "the latest developments in the region" with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.
US news site Axios reports that Cooper has been in the kingdom since Thursday, dealing with urgent coordination meetings as the situation in the Red Sea escalates.
US media outlets reported last week that President Trump had rejected a request by the crown prince for the US to directly intervene.
Despite turning down the request to unleash US firepower, Trump reportedly agreed to provide intelligence sharing and targeting assistance.
Iran war: Analyzing the Houthi blockade against Saudi Arabia
Iran blames Saudi Arabia for stalling Hormuz talks
Iran on Monday accused Saudi Arabia of delaying talks aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei called a meeting set to take place in Oman, a "real opportunity" to restore security in the region and added that an agreement between Iran and Oman on opening the passage had been finalized and would be announced later.
Saudi Arabia reportedly has concerns over the lasting implications of a deal for the Strait of Hormuz and how it might negatively impact Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries.
Tehran says Riyadh is using Yemen as a "pretext" to delay talks on how the Strait will be governed now that the status quo has been upended by the US.
Currently, the only secure routes allowing Saudi Arabia to deliver its oil to Asian markets are via the Suez Canal or around South Africa's Cape of Good Hope.
On Monday, China's Foreign Ministry called attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure "unacceptable," saying Beijing is "deeply concerned" about further escalation.
No sign of end to US-Iran conflict after six months

articles.title: Ukraine, Russia set for new round of US-mediated talks
articles.summary: New trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US could begin in October, according to Kyiv and Moscow. Few expect a breakthrough, but Ukraine is seeking a partial de-escalation to help it get…

image.caption: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has offered to meet with Vladimir Putin face-to-faceImage: Office of the President of Ukraine/B66/Avalon/Photoshot/picture alliance

blocks.text: Ukraine and Russia have signaled their readiness to resume trilateral talks under US mediation.
"We're preparing. For October," said Kyrylo Budanov, head of the Ukrainian president's office.
Similar signals came from Moscow: "We do not rule out such a possibility. We are talking about the foreseeable future," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner aimed to revive trilateral talks to end Russia's war in Ukraine, visiting Moscow and Kyiv in the first week of September.

The last round of trilateral talks took place in January and February 2026 in Abu Dhabi and Geneva, without producing a breakthrough, as the issue of territory control in eastern Ukraine remained unresolved.
Territory remains a difficult subject
Vladimir Putin still demands more territory than Russia currently controls, Kushner confirmed on September 12, speaking online at the YES security conference in Kyiv.

"President Putin [has] laid out his line of what he wants to achieve. If Ukraine wanted to withdraw to that line, then obviously we have the rest of the deal set up and put together. Ukraine right now does not want to do that," the US envoy said.

The Ukrainian government has indicated it is willing to freeze the fighting along the current frontline in exchange for security guarantees. Such a step could be supported by 60% of Ukrainians, according to a poll by the Kyiv International Institute of Sociology conducted in summer 2026. A similar majority of respondents rejected giving up territory that Russia hasn't been able to conquer. 33% said Ukraine should give up territory that Putin demands.
Russia's air superiority is a problem for Ukraine
Few expect a breakthrough anytime soon.

"For there to be a negotiated end to the war, there has to be parity. Right now, there's a stalemate on the front lines and not much is changing there, but in the air war, unfortunately, Russia currently has a significant advantage," Volodymyr Fesenko, a Kyiv-based political scientist, told DW.

Ukraine is running low on interceptors for Russian ballistic missiles. Russia has also stepped up attacks with new jet-powered drones, which fly faster than older gasoline-powered models and are harder to intercept.
Russia turns to jet-powered drones to wear Kyiv down
Russian airstrikes are increasingly targeting Ukraine's economy, including warehouses, energy facilities, gas stations and railway infrastructure.

The Kremlin has accused Ukraine of opening a "Pandora's box" by targeting Russia's economy and fuel and energy facilities with deep strikes since the summer. Ukraine says the attacks are intended to force Russia to the negotiating table.
Ukraine is worrying about the winter
Ukraine's supporters say Kyiv's strategy is working.

"The escalation ... is not a problem. It's a sign of success," said Jonathan Powell, the United Kingdom's National Security Adviser, speaking at the Yalta European Strategy conference in Kyiv on September 11. "Of course [Putin] doesn't go straight to negotiations, he tries to escalate in the ways that he can."
The West must "keep its foot on the gas" to make Putin negotiate in earnest, Powell said.

Such optimism contrasts with concerns in Ukraine about the upcoming winter. In 2025, Russian attacks on energy infrastructure caused extended blackouts and left people without heating in freezing temperatures.

"We anticipate a very difficult winter in terms of both critical infrastructure, which is being destroyed every day by Russian attacks, but also in terms of overall economic conditions in the country," said Ukraine's Economy Minister, Oleksandr Kravchenko.
Zelenskyy calls for partial de-escalation

Russia rejected the idea of a ceasefire during the upcoming talks. Ukraine is now calling for a de-escalation of attacks on energy infrastructure and the unblocking of grain exports via the Black Sea instead.

"What can bring us to any kind of negotiations? So, energy and grain. This is step number one. What we can achieve," Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told DW in an interview aired on September 12.
Zelenskyy backs Putin meeting at Miami G20: 'Results matter'

Political scientist Fesenko says an agreement on grain exports could prove the easier task: "In the Black Sea, both Ukraine and Russia are facing major problems. Grain exports have been blocked; ports have been shut down and therefore both sides have a stake in the matter."
An energy truce, however, remains elusive, as Ukraine's vulnerability in the winter gives Putin leverage he would not give up easily, Fesenko said.
At the same time, the US is increasing pressure on Ukraine to halt its attacks on Russian energy facilities.

"Mr. Zelenskyy has to do one thing: He has to ‌stop ⁠knocking out diesel fuel in Russia," Donald Trump said on Sunday, September 13. "There are plenty of other targets. Don't hit diesel fuel. That's hurting the world."
Kremlin rejected Zelenskyy-Putin meeting
The Kremlin has already rejected another of Zelenskyy's proposals: a meeting between the Ukrainian and Russian leaders in December on the sidelines of the G20 summit in Miami.

"Putin doesn't want to negotiate with Zelenskyy. It's been obvious since last year that he wants to reach an agreement with Trump," said Fesenko. "If Trump insists, Putin may agree to a meeting between the three leaders. But he has no intention of negotiating with Zelenskyy."
If negotiations start in October as expected, negotiating teams rather than the leaders themselves will conduct them. But Ukraine insists that only the presidents can decide the territorial issue.
"The territorial question remains a pressing one... Complex issues such as this are only resolved at the level of leaders," Zelenskyy said during the US envoys' visit to Kyiv.

articles.title: Crispin Odey loses appeal against lifetime ban from UK financial services industry
articles.summary:
Judges uphold ruling that financier tried to ‘frustrate’ investigations into harassment claims against him

The former hedge fund boss Crispin Odey has lost a legal challenge to overturn his…

blocks.text: The former hedge fund boss Crispin Odey has lost a legal challenge to overturn his lifetime ban from the City for trying to “frustrate” investigations into sexual harassment allegations against him.
A ruling by judges at the upper tribunal upheld the ban imposed by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) in March last year, while reducing a proposed fine of £1.83m to £1.53m.
“We have found that Mr Odey lacked integrity,” the tribunal ruling said, referring to the Conservative party donor’s behaviour at Odey Asset Management (OAM) between December 2021 and November 2022.
“Mr Odey is not a fit and proper person and it is reasonable for the authority to have concluded that a prohibition order is appropriate.”
Numerous allegations against Odey by female members of staff came to light after OAM launched an internal investigation into sexual harassment at the business in September 2020.

Odey, who resigned in 2023 after the allegations were reported in the media, tried to block executives of his hedge fund from taking any action, including by twice firing its entire executive committee (ExCos).
“He misused his power as controller to remove the ExCos as a means to protect his own interests and attempt to achieve his objectives,” the tribunal ruling said.

The judges also said the Brexit-backing hedge fund chief failed to acknowledge any potential harm during a three-week appeal hearing in March. “He has expressed no contrition,” they added. “He sees nothing wrong with his approach, and indeed he wrongly sees himself as the victim.”

The hearing involved a series of controversial admissions, including Odey blaming an incident in 2005 when he was alleged to have groped a colleague’s breasts on the effect of sedatives he had taken after root canal treatment. He said the woman had accepted his apology and continued to work for the firm for another eight years.
He also told the appeal judges he did not remember cornering a female employee after a boozy lunch and saying to her “I could attack you now”.
The allegations against Odey were first reported by the Financial Times in summer 2023. OAM ceased trading months later.
after newsletter promotion

Commenting on the ruling, the FCA’s executive director for enforcement and market oversight, Therese Chambers, said: “Mr Odey clearly thought he could act with impunity. He twice sacked those tasked with protecting female employees from his inappropriate behaviour when they tried to hold him to account. He felt the rules shouldn’t apply to him and acted to save his own skin.

“During the hearing he reinvented history, painted himself as a victim and displayed no contrition. That arrogant entitlement and the resulting complete disregard for proper governance means Mr Odey is unfit to work in financial services.”
Odey’s legal representatives were contacted for comment.

articles.title: Martin Romualdez in Quezon City Jail in Payatas
articles.summary: Former Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez has arrived at the Quezon City Jail, the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology has said.

blocks.text: Published September 14, 2026 11:11pm Updated September 14, 2026 11:19pm
Former Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez has arrived at the Quezon City Jail, the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology has said.
According to the BJMP, Romualdez arrived at the Payatas facility at 10:49 p.m.
He will undergo standard booking procedures: medical evaluation, fingerprint, mugshot, interview, and orientation.
Romualdez is facing plunder charges in connection with P7.2 billion in alleged kickbacks from government infrastructure projects.
His co-accused, former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co, Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp. president Felicito Guevarra, and Romualdez’s personal assistant Joselin Sereño are all at large.

Other officials facing plunder before the Sandiganbayan who are detained at the QC Jail in Payatas include Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta. Also in the said jail is former Anak Kalusugan party-list Rep. Michael Defensor.
In a statement, Romualdez said he respects the Sandiganbayan’s decision.
“I have always said that I will face the charges against me and answer them before the proper court. That has not changed,” he said.
“I maintain my innocence. Haharapin ko ang kaso. Sasagutin ko ang mga paratang,” he added.
(I maintain my innocence. I will face the case. I will answer the allegations.)
He also extended his gratitude to the doctors.
The Sandiganbayan on Monday committed Romualdez to the male dormitory of the Quezon City Jail.
He had been in the hospital since his arrest. First, in the Cardinal Santos Medical Center, and then in the Philippine General Hospital.
Doctors from the PGH on Monday told the Sandiganbayan that his condition was stable enough so as not to require being confined in the hospital.
In its order dated September 14, the Third Division also set his arraignment on Wednesday, September 16.

"Accordingly, the court commits to the Quezon City Jail - Male Dormitory the living person of accused Romualdez, who is charged for the crime of plunder, to be held therein as a detention prisoner and as such, the accused shall not be moved, removed, transferred, and/or otherwise be released therefrom unless ordered by the court," the court said.
"The parties are reminded that the arraignment and pre-trial of this case as to accused Romualdez si set on Wednesday, September 16, 2026 at 8:30 in the morning," it added. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: Women's Basketball World Cup: Can Germany harness a boom?
articles.summary: Germany thrilled fans at the Women's Basketball World Cup. But even if this sparked a boom in the women's game, the infrastructure simply isn't ready for it.

image.caption: Leonie Fiebich and her teammates thrilled German fans at the Women's Basketball World Cup in BerlinImage: sampics/picture alliance

blocks.text: The world's best players showcased their sport at the Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin, which wrapped up on September 13.

Germany, led by Leonie Fiebich and Nyara, improved with every game throughout the preliminary and intermediate round of the 10-day tournament. In the quarterfinals, Germany beat European champions Belgium, delivering what was arguably their best-ever performance.

The final weekend though, revealed the team still isn't quite ready to compete with the world's elite over a full 40 minutes. Germany lost to France in the semifinals before losing to Spain in the match for third place. Despite their disappointment, the Germans still saw the tournament as a huge success.
"We simply aren't good enough yet," said Fiebich after the Spain match.
"We played the tournament with a lot of euphoria and beat the European champions, Belgium. But it's hard to keep overperforming. Still, we will get better."

The World Cup marked a climax of the positive development seen in German women's basketball in recent years. In 2024, the team qualified for the Olympic Games for the first time, where the women also won a surprising gold in the 3x3 basketball. At the 2025 EuroBasket, Germany's women finished fifth. The next women's EuroBasket is next year and if Germany qualify, they should be medal contenders.
"I think it's important to harness the pain the players are feeling right now," Germany head coach Olaf Lange said.
"Because in our day-to-day work over the coming months and years, we need to improve individually. That requires a lot of motivation, and this pain acts as fuel for improvement."

The support from Germany fans could hardly have been greater. A total of around 230,000 tickets were sold for the World Cup and although visiting fans were present, the crowds were made up primarily of Germans.
Only three play for German clubs
While the national team is just a few steps away from establishing itself among the world's elite, Germany's top women's basketball league (DBBL) lags well behind the international competition.

Most players from the World Cup squad play abroad. Fiebich, Nyara Sabally and her sister Satou, who missed the tournament due to injury, as well as Luisa Geiselsöder and Frieda Bühner, play in the WNBA. Team captain Marie Gülich is moving to a club in Australia after the World Cup, having previously played in Taiwan. Emily Bessoir, Lina Sontag, and Alexis Peterson-Smalls play in Spain. Clara Bielefeld currently plays US college basketball.

blocks.caption: Frieda Bühner and the other Germany players enjoyed the attention of the Berlin fans Image: Tonhäuser/BEAUTIFUL SPORTS/picture alliance

blocks.text: Only three Germany players; Alexandra Wilke, Emma Eichmeyer, and Britta Daub, play for DBBL clubs, although both Eichmeyer and Daub have previously played abroad.
In Germany, they simply can't earn a living from playing basketball. Wilke, for example, works as a teacher at a secondary school.
DBBL level 'semi-professional'
Lange, who was a coach in the league from 1995 to 2002, describes it as "semi-professional," and says it has gone downhill since he left.
"Back then, the top clubs had better structures than they do today—and we are in 2026. That says it all. Things are really going backwards," he lamented during his post-tournament press conference.

blocks.caption: Olaf Lange's day job is as an assistant coach of the WNBA's Toronto TempoImage: Sammy Kogan/The Canadian Press/ZUMA/picture alliance

blocks.text: "I have to ensure that our top players go abroad. As long as nothing changes in the league, it will be difficult to sustain this success."
Professionalization efforts

Changes are needed to ensure the national team's continued success. Ireti Amojo took over as DBBL president in March. The former Germany player is a TV pundit and podcaster and has also worked in management of the women's program of top men's club ALBA Berlin. She has introduced several measures aimed to professionalize conditions at DBBL clubs.
"We aim to hire full-time youth development coaches. We also want to increase arena capacities," Amojo told daily newspaper TAZ prior to the World Cup.
"Currently, some venues hold a maximum of 600 spectators, and if interest grows – as it is now – we will need larger arenas."

blocks.caption: DBBL President Ireti Amojo is seeking to professionalize the leagueImage: Alexander Trienitz/nordphoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: 'Too late to capitalize on a World Cup boom'

However, the top division is not the whole story; even if the Women's Basketball World Cup were to trigger a surge of young girls taking up the game in Germany, most clubs would be ill-prepared to handle them. This is partly due to a shortage of coaches, but also because there is a lack of basketball facilities, making court time scarce.

"We should have started five years ago so that we could say now: 'We are capitalizing on the momentum of the World Cup and ensuring that all these kids who have become basketball fans can play the sport in clubs across Germany,'" Amojo told Magenta Sport after the World Cup final.

"We are too late. We lack the structures to harness this interest and provide all the children fascinated by basketball with the opportunity, under perfect training conditions, to develop into the next Leonie Fiebich or Nyara Sabally."
Still, Amojo thinks the World Cup may just prove to be a much-needed spark for future development.

"It was the kind of proof we all needed, because people are quick to dismiss it, claiming that no one in Germany is interested in women's basketball. Now we've seen that people in Germany are interested in women's basketball," she said.
"We already have a few levers we want to use to work on the structures. And this certainly shouldn't be the end of things."
This article was originally written in German.
