articles.title: Uganda reverses Invictus Games withdrawal after reassurance from King Charles
articles.summary:
Military chief had pulled country out over ‘Harry-Meghan nonsense’ but U-turned after clarification from the palace

Uganda has U-turned on its decision to withdraw from the Duke of Sussex’s…

blocks.text: Uganda has U-turned on its decision to withdraw from the Duke of Sussex’s Invictus Games after the country’s military chief said he had been reassured by King Charles that there was “no problem” with its participation.

Last week, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, the eldest son of the Ugandan president, Yoweri Museveni, made the surprise announcement the country would not participate in the games in a post on X. He said he was motivated by his respect for the king amid division over the “Harry-Meghan nonsense”.

However, a post on Monday from the spokesperson of the Uganda People’s Defence Force (UPDF), Chris Magezi, announced that Kainerugaba had reinstated Uganda’s participation in the 2027 Invictus Games, which will be held in Birmingham.
Magezi wrote that the shift was prompted by a telephone conversation between Kainerugaba and the principal private secretary to the king and queen, Clive Alderton.

Alderton had “revealed that King Charles III was moved by Gen Kainerugaba’s sensitive consideration of the king’s opinion on the upcoming Invictus Games organised by Prince Harry, the Duke of Sussex”.
He added that Charles “has no problem with Uganda’s participation in the Invictus Games, and encouraged the [Chief of Defence Forces] CDF to proceed with preparations”.
Kainerugaba “appreciated the king’s message and clarity provided by Buckingham Palace on the subject, promising that the UPDF would resume preparations to participate in the upcoming games”.

blocks.caption: Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, Uganda’s military chief, who initially announced the country’s withdrawal from the Invictus Games. Photograph: Abubaker Lubowa/Reuters

blocks.text: In the earlier post, Kainerugaba shared concerns that Uganda’s participation would be “construed as being opposed to his majesty King Charles III of the United Kingdom, whom we deeply revere”, adding that the country would “not participate in anything that does not have his majesty’s approval”.

The timing of the post led to speculation it was in response to an official letter to UK senior government and military officials on behalf of Charles that reiterated the Duke and Duchess of Sussex were not working royals and would not use their HRH styles.

The recent post stated instead that the withdrawal had followed a statement issued by Buckingham Palace indicating the Invictus Games were a private charity organisation. The king appeared at the 2014 launch of the Invictus Games, but the palace has not confirmed his attendance next year.

When asked by the Times about what had motivated the move, Kainerugaba is reported to have said: “I have factions in the Ministry of Defence that support that Harry-Meghan nonsense. I had to quash it straight away. I support the monarch. Period.”

Two months earlier, Harry had stood alongside Uganda’s defence minister, Kiryowa Kiwanuka, at an Invictus Games event in London to announce that the east African country would be the 26th country to enter the multisport event for wounded service personnel.
Kainerugaba, who, like Harry, is a graduate of the Royal Military Academy at Sandhurst, was appointed army chief in 2024 and is widely seen as his 81-year-old father’s successor to the presidency.

He has made several provocative posts on X, including threats to invade neighbouring Kenya, demands that Jay-Z hand over his wife, Beyoncé, so he could marry her, and threats against Bobi Wine, Museveni’s main political rival.

Rob Owen, the CEO of the Invictus Games Foundation, said: “We welcome the news that Uganda has confirmed it will continue to be part of the Invictus community and participate in the Invictus Games Birmingham 2027, now less than 300 days away.

“Uganda became our 26th nation earlier this year, joining a growing movement that provides year-round recovery opportunities for wounded, injured and sick service personnel and veterans across the world.”

articles.title: Martin Romualdez now in Payatas jail a week after arrest
articles.summary: (1st UPDATE) The Sandiganbayan 3rd Division ordered Romualdez's transfer of custody from PGH to Payatas after PGH doctors found that he is in stable condition and no longer in need of hospital…

blocks.text: PROBE. Leyte 1st District Representative Martin Romualdez appears before the Independent Commission for Infrastructure on October 14, 2025.
James Patrick Cruz/Rappler

(1st UPDATE) The Sandiganbayan 3rd Division ordered Romualdez's transfer of custody from PGH to Payatas after PGH doctors found that he is in stable condition and no longer in need of hospital confinement

items: Former speaker Martin Romualdez is detained at the New Quezon City Jail, following his arrest for plunder related to a flood control scandal.
He was transferred from the Philippine General Hospital to Payatas jail after doctors confirmed he was stable and no longer required hospital care.
Romualdez is scheduled for arraignment on September 16, where he will enter a plea regarding the charges against him.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Former speaker Martin Romualdez, the cousin of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., is now detained at the New Quezon City Jail a week after his arrest over plunder related to the multi-billion flood control scandal.
Romualdez was transferred to the Payatas jail at around 10:49 pm on Monday, September 14. This was confirmed to reporters by Bureau of Jail Management and Penology spokesperson Jayrex Bustinera.
Bustinera told Rappler Monday night that ongoing procedures for Romualdez include: “medical evaluation, fingerprint, mugshot, interview, and orientation.”

blocks.caption: Martin Romualdez now in Payatas jail a week after arrest

blocks.text: Earlier in the day, the Sandiganbayan 3rd Division ordered Romualdez’s transfer of custody from the Philippine General Hospital (PGH) to Payatas after PGH doctors found that the former speaker is in stable condition and no longer in need of hospital confinement.
PGH medical director Dr. Gerardo Legaspi said Romualdez has “no impending risk of heart attack.”

Romualdez was able to stall his Payatas detention for a week because he got confined in Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City before the issuance of a warrant. He also filed a motion before the 3rd Division to allow his continued hospital confinement.
The Court then held hearings to determine the real score on his health.
According to Romualdez’s attending physician and hematologist Dr. Rosalio Torres, he ordered the former speaker’s admission on September 7 due to the latter’s complaints about chest pain.

His admitting physician, Dr. Kurt Allen Sibayan, said Romualdez’s condition was not an emergency case and the lawmaker did not go through the emergency room. He also revealed that he was unable to see nor examine Romualdez because Torres barred him from entering the room.

On September 11, the division ordered Romualdez’s transfer from San Juan City to PGH to undergo independent medical examination. Legaspi said their team of experts finished the examination over the weekend and submitted their report to the court on Sunday.

Although they confirmed some illnesses like sleep apnea, hypertension, diabetes, and major depressive disorder, among others, Legaspi said the former speaker may already be discharged from confinement.
Romualdez will finally face the court on Wednesday, September 16, for his arraignment. This is the phase where the lawmaker will be read his case and will enter either a guilty or not guilty plea.
If Romualdez chooses to plead not guilty, the trial will proceed. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Oasis announce 2027 tour, including return to Knebworth 30 years after historic concerts
articles.summary:
After 2025’s wildly lucrative reunion, the Gallagher brothers will tour the UK, Ireland and US, and revisit the Hertfordshire site of their greatest live triumph

Oasis have finally confirmed…

blocks.text: Oasis have finally confirmed new tour dates for 2027, including their long-rumoured return to Knebworth for a run of shows 30 years after they played a historic two nights at the Hertfordshire venue in 1996.

“Start the celebrations!”, the band said in a statement. “After a period of reflection, The Most Damaging Pop Cultural Force In Recent British History” – a quote from a Guardian opinion piece about the band – “has declared itself fit for purpose and will once again return to lift the spirits of the people. Come witness the fitness. It shall be a sight to behold.”

Titled Oasis Live 27, the dates encompass the UK, Ireland, mainland Europe and the US, beginning in Glasgow on 21 May, and touring through Manchester, Munich, Barcelona, Amsterdam, Paris, Rome, Boston, Las Vegas and Slane Castle (north of Dublin), ending with four nights at Knebworth in September.
The band had teased the news in a massive drone display above Manchester’s Etihad stadium last week, after hinting at the dates on Instagram.

The tour follows Oasis’s acclaimed 2025 reunion, which saw them play 41 dates spanning the UK, Europe, North and South America, east Asia and Australia, 16 years after they split in 2009. “You struggle to think of another artist that’s received such a vociferous reception,” wrote Guardian critic Alexis Petridis in a five-star review of the first night of the tour in Cardiff.

The 2027 tour will be Oasis’s first visit to mainland Europe since their reunion and adds US cities they didn’t visit during that run. Their return to Paris will be particularly poignant, given it was shortly before a 2009 set at the city’s Rock en Seine festival that the band first split up.

In the UK, tickets will cost between £71.50 and £266.60. Those hoping to buy them will have a happier experience than those in the same position last year: all pricing information for Oasis Live 27 has been shared in advance after action by the competition watchdog forced Ticketmaster to change how it advertises tickets, including ending “misleading” information about seats, after fan backlash over its handling of the 2025 tour.

Last year, the use of “tiered” pricing meant that some fans, expecting to pay £148.50 per ticket, found themselves faced with costs of £350 at the checkout – and only a matter of minutes in which to decide whether to go ahead with their purchases. Now, Ticketmaster must tell fans 24 hours in advance if tiered pricing will be used, which tickets it covers and how the system works. When the sale is live, the price range must be shared and updated as tickets sell out.

Anyone wanting a ticket for 2027’s tour must register between now and 4pm BST on 17 September. The registration has been introduced “to reduce queuing times and organised ticket touting in order to give genuine fans the best possible chance to buy tickets,” according to organisers.

blocks.caption: Oasis pictured at Knebworth in 1996. Photograph: TCD/Prod.DB/Alamy

blocks.text: Fans had a chance to revisit the 2025 tour – or catch up on what they missed – as a documentary about the reunion, Don’t Look Back in Anger, hit cinemas last week after premiering at the Venice film festival. It earned glowing reviews for its emotional portrait of the band’s fans.

The documentary didn’t touch on the furore around ticket prices, other than one onstage comment from Liam Gallagher: after referring to the people in the cheap seats, he added: “Actually there are no cheap seats, sorry about that.”

The news that Oasis would return to Knebworth was first teased by an unlikely suspect, the British peer Baroness Taylor of Stevenage. In October 2025, she suggested in the House of Lords that Oasis would be playing five shows “in the fantastic venue of Knebworth House”, just a mile away from her own residence.

She quickly retracted her comments in the chamber, clarifying to the Guardian that she was “speaking hypothetically following speculation that they would play Knebworth again as they did in August 1996”.

In August, it was reported that SJM Concerts managing director Simon Moran had secured an events licence for Knebworth, prompting further speculation about an Oasis appearance. The licence would cover audiences of 125,000 people.

At the original 1996 dates, the band played to 250,000 fans – just one tenth of the number who applied for tickets, estimated at the time to be more than 4% of the entire British population. “This is history,” Noel Gallagher told the Knebworth crowd on the second night. The band recently started selling replicas of Noel and Liam’s respective outfits on the night.

A 2021 documentary, the prosaically titled Oasis Knebworth 1996, positioned the concerts as “the peak of British culture” wrote Guardian music editor Ben Beaumont-Thomas in a four-star review. The film’s voiceovers, he continued, implied that “all live music went downhill afterwards. It’s a lie every generation tells itself.” Liam subsequently headlined the park in June 2022.

UK Music estimated that the band’s five nights at Manchester’s Heaton Park last year led to music tourist spending in the north-west rising 16% year on year to £1.4bn. Momentum behind the tour was also credited with boosting the UK’s ongoing vinyl revival.
Oasis are also rumoured to be headlining Glastonbury 2027, the festival’s return after a fallow year in 2026.

Their reunion poured more fuel on the fire of enduring Britpop nostalgia, sparking a critically panned play documenting the rivalry between Oasis and Blur, an album called Britpop by Robbie Williams and even an embrace of Oasis in the US, a country that had been historically immune to their charms.

articles.title: Australia’s dependence on gas generation during evening energy peak falls by almost 70%
articles.summary:
Batteries now meet almost half of the grid’s dispatchable power needs during hours of highest demand

  • Get our

blocks.text: Australia’s dependence on gas for power during the evening, when the grid is under the most pressure, has fallen by almost nearly 70% over the past year as batteries surged in, replacing the fossil fuel.

Gas generation during the busy early evening, between 5pm and 8pm, fell by 67% in the year to August, as large-scale batteries continued to come online and half a million home batteries were installed under the government’s subsidy program, analysis by consultancy EnergyEdge found.
The company’s managing director, Josh Stabler, said batteries big and small recorded their highest peak output on record, off the back of rapid uptake.
“The rate of installation of batteries in Australia is the fastest uptake of any electricity asset ever – faster than solar, faster than wind,” he said.

According to the EnergyEdge report: “batteries have taken the evening peak, and they’re not giving it back”. Batteries met 49% of the grid’s dispatchable power needs during the evening in August 2026, up from 0.4% in 2020. In contrast, gas fell from 65.9% to 20.6% over the same period.
Wholesale electricity prices fell in response – a win for households – but potentially a problem for future investment in new dispatchable power.

Recent quarterly data (April to June) from the Australian Energy Market Operator highlighted a similar pattern, with gas generation recording its lowest Q2 on average in more than two decades. Gas power declined in all regions, the AEMO said, with the fall “most evident” during the evening peak.

The Grattan Institute’s energy and climate change program director, Alison Reeve, said utility scale batteries were increasingly mopping up surplus renewable energy in the middle of the day and displacing the role of gas during the peak.
“Overall, this is super good news. What you actually end up doing is flattening out the load curve over the day,” she said, and that reduced volatility in the system.

In the longer term, less gas and lower volatility should be good for prices, she said. Although the declining demand and added uncertainty could make gas more expensive and less profitable at those times when it was needed – in those few dark, still and cold weeks in winter.

“That’s kind of the challenge that is coming for gas,” she said. “We know that gas generators are going to be important, because they’re going to be the backup when you get those two weeks in winter where solar, wind and batteries can’t carry you through.”

AEMO’s 20-year roadmap, the Integrated System Plan, anticipated gas would play “a more strategic, back-up role, with flexible generators that can also provide system security service” in future. “This is more likely to be in winter, especially in the southern states, when shorter days reduce solar output, and when more electricity is needed for longer and colder nights.

“Gas is going through a transition and its whole role is going to change,” Reeve said, a shift that would affect the amount of gas needed, the number of generators and the running costs. “The sooner that we actually grasp that the future for gas generators is going to look nothing like the past, the better we will be at managing that whole process and making sure it doesn’t end up costing people a lot of money.”

articles.title: Cloudy with a chance of rainbow: iridescent clouds brighten the sky over parts of Victoria
articles.summary: Rainbow clouds are not uncommon in Australia but rarely photographed, and experts say they get their colours when light is diffracted around ice crystals

blocks.text: Rainbow clouds shone over parts of Victoria over the weekend, in an unusual visual phenomenon known as iridescent clouds.
Photographs of the spectacle were taken by onlookers in the Melbourne suburbs of Mount Waverley and Caroline Springs.
Sarah Scully, a senior meteorologist at the Bureau of Meteorology, said the visual phenomenon was not uncommon in Australia but was rarely captured.
“People don’t often notice them, as they’re really fleeting,” she said.

Iridescent clouds often form from cirrus clouds, which were seen over Victoria on the weekend. Cirrus clouds are made up of ice crystals and are commonly found in the higher levels of the troposphere – the level of the atmosphere where most weather occurs – where the temperatures are coldest.

blocks.caption: Rainbow clouds often form from cirrus clouds. Photograph: Amruta Wazalwar

blocks.text: The clouds get their rainbow appearance when light is diffracted – bent – around ice crystals. The phenomenon often occurs in newly formed clouds where the ice crystals are the same size.
The smaller the cloud, the more rays of sunlight can pass through and be diffracted by a single ice droplet, according to the BoM.
Iridescent clouds gain their appearance from the diffraction of sunlight, which causes the colours to spread into rings or waves.
They differ from rainbows, in which both the refraction (bending) and reflection (bouncing back) of sunlight result in colours in a specific order with neater bands.
after newsletter promotion
Iridescent clouds are sometimes mistaken for sun dogs, another type of visual phenomenon with similar characteristics.
“Sun dogs are a different type of optical phenomenon,” Scully said. “They occur almost like a pillar of light that’s either on both sides of the sun or just on one side of the sun.”
“That is due … to water crystals being in the atmosphere, and … it sits at low levels of the horizon. You need it to sit even lower [than an iridescent cloud],” Scully said.

articles.title: Gonorrhoea and syphilis rise by more than 50% in Australia with ‘concerning’ rise in cases in women
articles.summary:
Newly collated data also shows Indigenous Australians experiencing disproportionally high rates of infection

  • Get our

blocks.text: Rates of reported gonorrhoea and infectious syphilis have increased by more than 50% across Australia over the past decade, with experts warning of concerning rises among women.

Newly collated sexual health data from UNSW’s Kirby Institute shows 42,393 gonorrhoea notifications and 5,986 infectious syphilis notifications were recorded in 2025. The figures represent 10-year increases of 57% and 56%, respectively.
Syphilis and gonorrhoea are bacterial infections that can cause serious health complications if left untreated. Both are curable when detected early.

Men accounted for the majority of cases last year, making up 73% of gonorrhoea notifications and 78% of infectious syphilis notifications, with the report suggesting a significant proportion of transmission continues to occur through male-to-male sexual contact among gay and bisexual men.

The new data also flagged a “concerning increase in syphilis among women”. Syphilis notification rates increased by 167% among women, compared with 39% among men. Experts said the figures reflected “an increase in heterosexual transmission”.
Dr Skye McGregor, an epidemiologist at the Kirby Institute, said the trend is “an urgent priority” because of the risks posed by syphilis during pregnancy.

“It’s really concerning because the rise among women has contributed to syphilis in pregnancy, which can cause miscarriage, stillbirth, congenital syphilis and infant deaths. These are really substantial impacts on infants, but also the community as a whole. Across that same 10-year reporting period, there were 113 congenital syphilis cases and, tragically, 40 of those infants died,” McGregor said.
Around half of those congenital syphilis cases involved Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander infants.
“A really terrible outcome, which is entirely preventable with early testing and treatment during pregnancy,” McGregor said.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Australians also remain a priority group, experiencing disproportionately high sexually transmitted infection (STI) rates. Compared with non-Indigenous Australians, the Indigenous population is diagnosed with gonorrhoea at more than four times the rate and syphilis at more than six times the rate.
after newsletter promotion

McGregor said the disparity highlighted the need for sustained investment in culturally safe sexual health services and improved access to timely testing and treatment, particularly in regional and remote areas.

“We know how hard it can be to get an appointment in an urban setting with a GP, particularly if you want a preferred provider by gender or cultural background. And that’s even more exacerbated in regional and remote settings,” she said.
McGregor said social determinants of health also contributed to the disparity, including income, education, employment, job security and food insecurity.
She stressed the importance of culturally safe sexual health testing services and community-led programs supported by the National Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisation and governments.

“Modelling has predicted that without that enhanced response, actually the rates of syphilis would have been far higher …this amazing community-driven response has actually ensured that the rates do stay lower than they could have been across that time period,” McGregor said.

McGregor said the new data should serve as a public health reminder of the importance of testing and treatment, raising concerns that reduced testing could be an unwanted hangover from the Covid-19 pandemic.
“We saw a decrease during that time period, but we really need to make sure everyone’s resuming their pre-Covid screening so that sexual health is just a part of good health overall,” she said.

UNSW’s 2019 National Debrief Survey looking into sexual health attitude revealed that almost two-thirds of young people who had five or more casual partners in the past 12 months did not use condoms. But McGregor said reducing STI rates required a holistic approach.

“Condoms are still an important prevention approach, and yes, people should be using condoms with new sexual partners … but also, this is about comprehensive prevention,” she said. “Early testing ensures people know their status, they can be treated, prevent onward transmission.”
McGregor also stressed the importance of “post-diagnosis care”, retesting and regular engagement with a healthcare provider, as “we do know that one infection then risks a repeat infection”.

articles.title: Queensland homeless man shot with Taser after being given move-on order to make way for kite festival
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Advocate says homeless clearances should be halted after man is hospitalised during confrontation in Brisbane park

  • Get our

blocks.text: A homeless man was shot with a Taser by police after attempting to take his own life during a tent city clearance, sparking calls for mental health considerations when dealing with move-on orders amid Queensland’s homelessness crisis.

On 1 September, Moreton Bay city council rangers gave six homeless residents 24 hours to leave Pelican Park north of Brisbane, where Martin* had been living in a camper trailer, to make way for a kite festival this weekend.
The 48-year-old said he was unable to comply with the move-on order because he had lost his driver licence due to a drink-driving conviction.
“I was under the understanding that they were coming to basically take my shit,” he told the Guardian. “In times gone past, I’ve complied.
“This time I can’t, and they told me that basically they’re going to impound everything.”
The homeless man, who has prostate cancer, told the rangers he would rather die than lose his few possessions.
“I said, ‘All right, well, if this is what you wish to do, then not a problem. Bring an ambulance and a body bag for me,’” Martin said.
He then stabbed himself in the neck with a knife. Moments later he was shot with a Taser at least twice by police.
He said he had not threatened anyone else before injuring himself.
A spokesperson for the Queensland police said its officers had attempted to de-escalate the situation and disarm Martin, but were unsuccessful.
“Immediate first aid was applied by officers to the man, who had sustained a serious self-inflicted injury,” they said.

“The QPS remains committed to providing officers with mental health training, focusing on an informed awareness of different categories of mental illness and the application of appropriate strategies to safely respond to persons experiencing mental health distress.”

Local homeless advocate Beau Haywood, founder of charity Nourish Street, said the incident showed what can go wrong if councils continued their enforcement-led approach to the state’s homelessness crisis. He said Moreton Bay should halt homeless clearances until they could show they were both safe and legal.
Snapping point

Martin, whose camp is part of a small tent city of about a dozen residents near the waterfront in Clontarf, is a former security guard who lost his job during the pandemic. He has lived homeless in the Moreton Bay area for more than three years, and is on the social housing waiting list.

He’s not alone: Moreton Bay has the state’s longest social housing waiting list – 5,146 at last count in 2025 – and a major rough sleeping problem. Several tent cities in the area house hundreds of people.

He said after it happened he woke up in an ambulance on the way to the Royal Brisbane and Women’s hospital. He had surgery to patch up his injuries, saw a mental health worker, and asked to be discharged so he could get back to his camper trailer to protect his belongings.
The next day, the hospital booked him a taxi back to the park.
He had not been seen by any health professional since his discharge, he said.
after newsletter promotion
A spokesperson for the Metro North health service said it was “unable to comment on the specific details of a patient’s situation to respect their privacy and confidentiality”.

Moreton Bay was the first of many councils across the country to turn to enforcement as the solution to Australia’s worsening homelessness crisis. It made national headlines when it bulldozed a tent city in Lawnton, which the Queensland supreme court ruled a violation of the state’s Human Rights Act.
Haywood said the council had halted clearances during and after the court case, but had recently restarted them after announcing it would designate a park for the homeless.
Haywood said during clearances, homeless people like Martin could feel backed into a corner and it was inevitable that people would eventually snap.
“I’ve seen it time and time again. Every move brings [someone’s mental health] down even further . And I think for that gentleman, he reached his point,” he said.
“I think that if council were aware of his mental health and physical health, that maybe some more precautions should be taken. Some mental health treatment should have been offered at the time.”
Haywood said the clearances should be halted until they could be done safely.

Martin said he loved old movies, motorcycles and a long chat. He has refused treatment for his prostate cancer. He said before he died he wanted to see friends in Townsville and South Australia. He said one of his greatest joys was to cook for his homeless friends.
Since the confrontation, Martin’s circumstances have not changed. He has not been offered housing, or an alternative place to stay.
There are 44,294 Queenslanders on the social housing waiting list.
A homeless service hopes to tow his vehicle to a different park this week.
*Name has been changed

articles.title: One Nation under fire for abandoning gas reservation plan in favour of policy benefiting Gina Rinehart
articles.summary:
Pauline Hanson’s gas policy and the party’s relationship with Rinehart is examined in a new Guardian podcast series, The Populist

  • Listen:

blocks.text: One Nation has come under fire for quietly shelving support for a new domestic gas reservation policy in preference for a policy that favours the party’s billionaire patron, Gina Rinehart.

The Albanese government has announced it will establish a new reservation policy for Australia’s east coast, requiring gas exporters to supply a portion of the gas they produce to the domestic market. The policy is aimed at “modestly” supplying the domestic market to put downward pressure on prices for consumers.
Pauline Hanson moved a Senate motion as recently as March in support of a domestic gas reserve, saying it would “increase the supply of gas and lower the price of electricity directly”.
But the reservation plan has been vehemently opposed by Senex, a $900m company that is 49% owned by Rinehart’s Hancock Prospecting, and 51% owned by the Korean company POSCO.

In June, One Nation abandoned its longstanding support when it unveiled its gas plans after “consultation with industry and stakeholders” saying the policy risked “killing domestic Australian gas companies”.
The Guardian has been examining Hanson’s gas policy and the party’s relationship with Rinehart in a new podcast series on One Nation, The Populist.
The resources minister, Madeleine King, told the Guardian that One Nation’s decision to abandon its policy suggested it was influenced by the industry’s position.
“One Nation was hoping nobody would notice they had abandoned any form of gas reservation policy,” King said.
“One Nation claims to support Aussie families but the truth is they are always on the side of their big business backers.”
The Coalition is considering supporting the proposal, while the Greens are pushing for a 25% gas export tax instead.
The opposition spokesperson for energy affordability and security, Garth Hamilton, said that the party had “dramatically” changed its position to one that benefited Senex and Rinehart.
“This policy backflip must be for the benefit of her donors, because it is not for the benefit of the Australian people,” he said.
In One Nation’s policy statement in June, it said: “One Nation has previously considered an East Coast gas reservation policy”.

“However, through consultation with industry and stakeholders, it became clear that it fell short of our policy objectives. The government’s 20% reservation policy will damage onshore development of oil and gas projects.”
In April, the party received the gift of a new aircraft worth up to $2m from Hancock Prospecting and $1m in donations from two of Rinehart’s closest associates.
One Nation claims that its policy to encourage joint ventures between government and industry was “effectively removing the need for a reservation policy that risks distorting the market”.
after newsletter promotion
Rinehart and the former Liberal leader Peter Dutton had a disagreement in the lead-up to the last election over the Liberal party’s plan for an east coast gas reservation policy.

In a Senate estimates exchange in June, the One Nation senator Tyron Whitten asked departmental officials about the reservation policy saying the party had “heard from industry that the oversupply model is going to make onshore exploration and development almost impossible economically”.
The Greens senator Steph Hodgins-May challenged Whitten for “asking questions on behalf of Senex, which is co-owned by Gina Rinehart”.
Whitten said: “I can’t be asking questions on behalf of Gina Rinehart. I’ve never met the lady.”
A spokesperson for Senex said the company and other businesses “engage with all sides of politics to inform policy development and help improve living standards for Australians”.
The social services minister, Tanya Plibersek, also took aim at the party, after revelations in the Guardian’s podcast The Populist about Joyce and Hanson staying overnight at her Brisbane mansion.
Plibersek accused One Nation of “just doing Gina Rinehart’s bidding”.
“We’ve seen now that Barnaby’s having sleepovers at Gina’s, he’s being flown around the country in the private jet because he’s doing her bidding,” she said on Monday.

“She’s more than just a friend. She is One Nation’s biggest donor. So, when it comes to same jobs, same pay, making sure people who work in mining, for example, get paid the same, she says no. Gina says no. So One Nation says no.
“When it comes to attacking Andrew Hastie, Gina doesn’t like him. So One Nation doesn’t like him. They attack Andrew Hastie.”

articles.title: Body of missing runner found in South Africa: 'It is very scary'
articles.summary: A nationwide appeal was launched after Elizabeth Moselakgomo went missing last week. Four other women's bodies have been found nearby.

blocks.text: South African police have confirmed the death of a jogger, who went missing during a routine run last week, sparking a nationwide appeal for help finding her.

The body of Elizabeth Moselakgomo was identified by her relatives on Monday after it was discovered east of Johannesburg on Saturday. She is one of five women whose bodies have been found half-naked and bruised in the same area, Kempton Park.
Police said they were not linking the deaths to a serial killer but added that the "similarities are sufficiently concerning… to issue a public warning".
A jogger who knew Moselakgomo through their running club told the BBC the discovery of the five bodies was "very scary".
"It's sad to know that every woman in South Africa… can't just go outside. You can't just go to the shop and buy flowers… because you are always in danger," said Keamo Sefularo.
Police have urged women in the Kempton Park area to avoid walking or running alone "particularly in isolated areas".
South Africa experiences some of the world's highest levels of gender-based violence (GBV), with the rate at which women are killed five times higher than the global average, according to UN Women.
Moselakgomo's body was found on Saturday night, badly bruised and partially clothed.
Just hours earlier on Monday, another woman's half-naked body was found about 25km (15 miles) away.
The latest discovery was made by a passer-by, who spotted the body on his way to work, police spokesperson Brig Athlenda Mathe told reporters at the scene.
One arrest has been made in connection with the discovery of the first body. The person is still in police custody.
The police have since set up a task team to investigate the murders but these grim discoveries and Moselakgomo's death have sparked renewed outrage and fear among South Africans.
Tributes poured in for the avid runner, affectionately known as "Tsontso" after police confirmed her death. South Africans also shared the fear and anxiety women often feel in the country.
Lesedi Ledwaba, in a post on X, said: "Women are not free if we have to calculate where, when and with whom we can walk, run or exist safely".
This was echoed by Sefularo, who said Moselakgomo's disappearance had been "heavy for the club".
The 29-year-old also asked whether Moselakgomo would "still be here if maybe she had a small community to run with [or] one or three people"?
"As we always say, when we go out for runs, there's safety in numbers," she reflected.
Sefularo shared the measures she often took to keep safe while running, including avoiding taking the same route each day and making sure she ran in areas with good visibility.
Advocacy group Women for Change said the discovery of these bodies was angering.
"What is the purpose of having a protective service like the police if we have to make sure… we are [protecting] ourselves," the group's Merlize Jogiat asked.
Jogiat mostly blamed poor implementation of laws passed for the failure to curb the issue and said "pressure in numbers" from citizens could be the solution.
Moselakgomo's family thanked the public for the support in searching for the mother of one and commended her eight-year-old daughter for raising the alarm about her disappearance.
Authorities are yet to identify the remaining bodies.

articles.title: Undisputed Lanao del Sur 8th District bet takes BARMM seat
articles.summary: Ahmad 'Arrie' Balindong will continue his stay as a member of parliament in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao

blocks.text: BARMM POLLS. Member of Parliament Ahmad Amir Balindong is the bet of the United Bangsamoro Justice Party for the 8th District of Lanao del Sur.
Ahmad Amir Balindong's Facebook page
Ahmad 'Arrie' Balindong will continue his stay as a member of parliament in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao
COTABATO CITY, Philippines – Member of Parliament (MP) Ahmad “Arrie” Balindong will be 8th District representative of Lanao del Sur after running undisputed in the Bangsamoro parliamentary polls.
Balindong has received 72,093 votes, according to 93.82% of total election returns, as of September 14, 10:14 pm.
He ran under the banner of the United Bangsamoro Justice Party, which is led by Ahod “Al Haj Murad” Ebrahim, chairman of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front.

Prior to the campaign, Balindong was appointed a member of the Bangsamoro Parliament by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in March 2025. He served as vice chairperson of the committee on agriculture, fisheries, and agrarian reform, and the committee on environment, natural resources, and energy.

He comes from the Balindong political dynasty, which traces its roots to the late Sultan Amer Macaorao Balindong, former mayor of Malabang in Lanao del Sur, the father of the late Bangsamoro parliament speaker Pangalian Balindong. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Polls to resume in Maluso, Basilan on Sept. 15 after ballot incident
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Commission on Elections (Comelec) on Monday said the conduct of the first Bangsamoro Parliamentary elections will resume in Maluso, Basilan on Tuesday, Sept. 15, after…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Commission on Elections (Comelec) on Monday said the conduct of the first Bangsamoro Parliamentary elections will resume in Maluso, Basilan on Tuesday, Sept. 15, after flagging reports of compromised ballots.
According to Comelec chair George Erwin Garcia, the voting period will still run from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.

“The same general instruction ang ipapatupad natin at therefore inaasahan natin na more or less mga 8 ng gabi ay tapos na yung pagbilang doon at pag-transmit ng results,” Garcia said in a press briefing.
(We will implement the same general instruction and therefore we expect that more or less, the counting of votes and transmission of results will be done by 8 p.m.)
He then maintained that it is just a continuation of the elections, and not a postponement.
This came after the Comelec discovered that the ballots of 36 out of 68 polling precincts in the Basilan town were already pre-shaded.

The Comelec then ordered the reprinting of over 16,000 ballots in the National Printing Office. Garcia said that estimated arrival of the ballots from Manila to Zamboanga was around 4 p.m. but it was delayed for two hours.
He added that the ballots would be transferred from Zamboanga to Basilan. He noted that the reprinted ballots will be distributed to electoral board members on early Tuesday morning.
Garcia also said that winners in areas not affected by the incident in Masulo can already be proclaimed late Monday evening.
As of 9:42 p.m., the Comelec already received 91.4% of the total election returns (ERs). This is equivalent to 4,764 out of 5,212 ERs. /cb

articles.summary: Arimao Asum, patriarch of the Asum political dynasty in Lumbayanague, Lanao del Sur, leads the race for the province's 5th District seat in the first elections of the Bangsamoro Parliament

blocks.text: BARMM POLLS. Arimao Asum, a former vice mayor of Lumbayanague, is the head patriarch of the Asum political dynasty.
Arimao Asum's Facebook page
Arimao Asum, patriarch of the Asum political dynasty in Lumbayanague, Lanao del Sur, leads the race for the province's 5th District seat in the first elections of the Bangsamoro Parliament

COTABATO CITY, Philippines – Arimao Asum, a former vice mayor of Lumbayanague and patriarch of the Asum political dynasty, is set to win the 5th District seat of Lanao del Sur during the Bangsamoro parliamentary elections.
Asum has received 43,316 votes, according to 93.38% of total election returns as of September 14, 10:14 pm.

He holds a wide lead over his closest competitor, former Tubaran mayor and United Bangsamoro Justice Party bet Khaledyassin Papandayan, with 28,059 votes. Trailing the race is independent candidate Udtog Tago with 1,229 votes.

Asum is the bet of the Serbisyong Inklusibo-Alyansang Progresibo Party, which is led by Lanao del Sur Governor Mamintal Adiong Jr. and his son, Lanao del Sur Vice Governor Mohammad Khalid Adiong. He is also the father of incumbent Lumbayanague Mayor Jamal Asum and the husband of Vice Mayor Salamona Asum. – Rappler.com

articles.summary:
Samusocial de Paris documents signs of violence after detention and transfer under ‘one in one out’ scheme

Multiple injuries including bruising and fractures have been documented by a health…

blocks.text: Multiple injuries including bruising and fractures have been documented by a health service supporting people returned to France under the controversial “one in, one out” scheme.

The pilot scheme involves one asylum seeker who crosses the Channel in a small boat being returned to France in return for another in northern France being legally brought to the UK to claim asylum. The scheme is due to end on 1 October.

Samusocial de Paris (SSP) has been commissioned by Île-de-France’s regional health agency to provide healthcare for asylum seekers returned to France in the first eight days after their deportation from the UK, when they are accommodated in a shelter in Paris.

They have documented the cases of 90 returnees between 22 January and 7 June 2026. All are young men, mostly in their 20s and early-30s, who sought sanctuary in the UK after fleeing a variety of conflict zones including Eritrea, Sudan and Afghanistan.
About 1,400 people have been forcibly removed to France by the Home Office since the scheme began in August 2025, although some have subsequently returned to the UK in lorries or small boats.

The evidence compiled by SSP has been submitted to the French Assembly’s cross-party inquiry into the impact of the Anglo-French border deals known as Le Touquet agreements. This evidence comes from their own clinical consultations with returnees and some hospital reports from those sent to A&E.

Many of those detained in the UK for “one in one out” have fled torture and other forms of persecution in their home countries, and have been subjected to modern slavery on their journeys in countries such as Libya. However, the focus of the report is on what happened to people while they were detained in the UK as part of the scheme and during their removal to France.

blocks.caption: People wade into the water at Gravelines, France, hoping to board a small boat to the UK. Photograph: Dan Kitwood/Getty Images

blocks.text: According to the report: “Consultations are revealing signs consistent with recent physical and psychological violence as well as the consequences of prolonged detention in conditions described as particularly degrading.” It states that the physical and psychological conditions documented are “explicitly linked to the implementation of the France-British agreement”.
The report adds: “The frequency and recurrence of the incidents reported by people transferred under the Franco-British agreement appear particularly worrying.”

One A&E medical report from a returnee who arrived in France in such a bad state that he was sent to hospital reads: “The patient’s general condition was marked by significant suffering and shock upon arrival necessitating referral to the hospital emergency department. The medical certificate mentions reports of physical violence in England, including diffuse bruising, injuries consistent with restraint (lacerations with handcuffs) and abdominal pain resulting from repeated blows.”

The report includes 13 case studies documenting a range of injuries, including problems that worsened due to a lack of medical treatment, while people were in detention in the UK. Concerns were also raised about mental health conditions such as PTSD.

In one case, a man was referred for emergency psychiatric treatment because he was too disoriented to find his way back to the dormitory while in the shelter, suffered from body tics and incoherent speech and was deemed to be at risk of suicide. The report highlights limited options for ongoing psychiatric treatment for this group.

SSP recommends that a mechanism should be established to collect information on allegations of mistreatment by the British authorities that can be sent to the UK. It also suggests reporting this issue to the French prosecutor under Article 40 of the French code of criminal procedure.

Nihal Osman, a programme coordinator for Médecins Sans Frontières, which also provides health support for this group of returnees, said: “This one in one out agreement is a machine for psychological destruction.

“The deeply concerning physical injuries sustained whilst in detention in the United Kingdom, which we have documented among those deported, must be viewed in the light of a serious psychological deterioration.”
The UK Home Office and the company Mitie, which provides the guards for the asylum seekers, have been approached for comment.

articles.title: Defense couldn't 'sabotage' Cabotaje-Tang, says prosecution
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte's team failed in its efforts to "sabotage" retired Sandiganbayan Presiding Justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang's testimony, the House prosecution panel said.

blocks.text: VP SARA DUTERTE IMPEACHMENT TRIAL
Published September 14, 2026 10:37pm

The defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte failed in its efforts to "sabotage" the testimony of retired Sandiganbayan Presiding Justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang, the House prosecution panel said Monday.
Cabotaje-Tang, who retired in 2024, has 44 years of experience handling anti-corruption cases from the Supreme Court and the Office of the Solicitor General up to the Sandiganbayan.
She testified at the impeachment trial as an expert on anti-corruption and accountability laws governing officials and their associates, after she was subpoenaed by the prosecution to appear.

“Hindi nasabotahe si Cabotaje-Tang [They were not able to sabotage Cabotaje-Tang]. She served the government for 44 years, she testified why the SALN [Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth] reporting for public officials is important, why honesty weighs a lot, especially for high-ranking public officials, and why public officials should be transparent and accountable for their wealth,” said House prosecutor Terry Ridon of Bicol Saro party-list in a press conference after the day's trial proceedings.

“Our witness has her credibility intact, and I will repeat what many of the senator judges had stated. We thank her for the service to the nation, and we thank her today for basically delivering the message that public office is a public trust,” he added.

The defense initially objected to Cabotaje-Tang’s testimony, calling it irrelevant. On the stand,she fielded the defense's questions on whether she received compensation for her testimony, if she was anti-Duterte, or if she "liked" the Vice President.
Expert on accountability

Asked if the questions posed by the defense team to Cabotaje-Tang were disrespectful, House prosecutor Chel Diokno of Akbayan party-list did not give a categorical answer but said the prosecution was able to establish, through her testimony, that public officials are ultimately accountable to the people who elected them.
"Kayo na lang po ang maghusga diyan [You be the judge],” said Diokno, who conducted a direct examination on Cabotaje-Tang on the stand.

“It is pretty clear that our purpose is to present the legal framework [for our impeachment case], and that is why we had her as a witness. She is the best person to explain the things needed to be explained,” Diokno added.
Among the salient points of Cabotaje-Tang’s testimony which cited existing anti-corruption laws and Supreme Court decisions include:

items: a public official with proven unexplained wealth can be removed from office
cash on hand and cash in bank should be declared under cash category of the SALN, not under “others”

government authorities can scrutinize the wealth of the public official’s immediate family such as spouse and children because this will prevent public officials from using their family members to hide their money
laws require a public official to declare his or her spouse’s assets under his/her SALN unless they have a prenuptial agreement of separation of assets.

blocks.text: For Deputy Speaker Janette Garin, defense lawyer Mark Vinluan’s questioning during the cross-examination was improper.

“It was very disrespectful and uncalled for. If they really wanted to test her credibility, then they should have presented a case wherein the former justice was involved in a bribery case. Wala [naman] e. We cannot deny that the reputation of our former Sandiganbayan Presiding Justice is untainted by such,” she said.
(There was none presented of that kind.)

“She was there to interpret laws to the best of her capability and her experience having been in government in those positions [addressing corruption] for a long time. And I am sorry, but in my view, sa bagong Pilipinas, bawal ang bastos, at kanina, medyo nababastusan ako roon sa ibang katanungan ni Attorney Mark Vinluan [In the new Philippines, disrespect is not allowed, and I found some of Attorney Vinluan's questions disrespectful],” Garin added. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Trump’s EPA reportedly ⁠poised to axe carbon pollution rules for power plants
articles.summary:
Advocates and experts describe the Trump administration’s climate rollbacks as gifts to polluters at expense of planet

The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is ⁠poised to formally…

blocks.text: The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is ⁠poised to formally repeal carbon pollution standards for coal- and gas-fired power plants, according to reports.

The Trump administration’s latest climate rollback is expected to ⁠come as soon as Monday on the sidelines of the G20 energy ministers’ meeting in Houston, ⁠Texas, Bloomberg News reported on Sunday, citing anonymous sources familiar with the matter.

Lee Zeldin, the EPA administrator, is expected to announce the move in Houston to erase the planet-heating pollution that gets pumped into the air during oil and gas burning, the New York Times reported.
Such a move would almost certainly face legal challenges but if it survived, this rollback of pollution standards could reduce the agency of future administrations to control climate emissions.
Environmental groups condemned the expected move.

“The Sierra Club will fight back against this reckless and dangerous proposal with everything we have in the courts, in Congress, and in communities across the country,” said Holly Bender, the Sierra Club’s chief program officer.

She added: “While wildfires rage, floods devastate communities, and families struggle to afford skyrocketing electricity bills and insurance premiums, the Trump administration is handing the fossil fuel industry a license to keep polluting. This is full-throated climate denial while the climate crisis happens in real time and a shocking betrayal of the American public.”
Last year, Donald Trump’s ​administration proposed repealing rules ‌passed under Joe Biden to curb emissions of carbon dioxide, mercury ‌and other air pollutants from power plants.

This week, the EPA is finalizing a piece of the initial proposal, and agency officials also plan to propose a separate rule repealing the federal finding that greenhouse gases ‌from power plants specifically pose a threat, Bloomberg said.
The EPA did not respond to a request for comment outside business hours.

Trump has long backed promoting the interests of oil and gas and has stepped up efforts in his second term in the White House to remove environmental regulations he argues are unnecessary barriers to industrial development and expanded energy ​production.
Climate advocates and experts have described the rollbacks as gifts to polluters at the expense of the planet, Americans’ public health and economic wellbeing.
Biden’s carbon ​emission rules for ​power plants would have reduced greenhouse gas emissions ​by 1bn metric tons ​by 2047, ​a crucial part of his administration’s fight against the climate crisis.
The electricity sector is responsible for nearly a quarter of US greenhouse gas pollution.
Reuters contributed reporting

blocks.text: BARMM POLLS. Abdul Rauf Adiong is the nephew of Lanao del Sur Governor Mamintal Adiong Jr. and the bet of the Serbisyong Inklusibo-Alyansang Progresibo Party in Lanao del Sur's third parliamentary district.
Abdul Rauf Adiong Facebook Page
Serbisyong Inklusibo-Alyansang Progresibo Party bet Abdul Raud Adiong wins against two former members of the Bangsamoro Parliament and a former village chief

COTABATO CITY, Philippines – Abdul Rauf Adiong, nephew of Lanao del Sur Governor Mamintal Adiong Jr., is on the verge of winning the province’s 3rd District seat in the Bangsamoro parliamentary elections.
Adiong has received 54,454 votes, according to 92.38% of total election returns, as of September 14, 9:59 pm.

He holds a wide lead over his closest competitor, independent candidate Edrieza Rimbang, who has 19,521 votes. Currently in third place is United Bangsamoro Justice Party bet Jamel Ditucalan Macaraya with 7,347 votes, while independent candidate Sittie Saleha Mangurun trails the race with 285 votes.
Both Macaraya and Rimbang were former members of the Bangsamoro Parliament, while Mangurun is a former barangay chairperson of Malinao in Tagoloan.

Adiong ran under his uncle’s party, the Serbisyong Inklusibo-Alyansang Progresibo Party. The Adiong scion is the son of Ditsaan-Ramain Mayor Ansaruddin Abdul Malik Alonto Adiong and the grandson of the late former Lanao del Sur governor Mamintal Adiong Sr. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Gandamra dynasty matriarch set to take Marawi’s BARMM seat
articles.summary: Princess Pala Gandamra, the wife of Marawi Vice Mayor Majul Gandamra, is enjoying an overwhelming lead in the race to represent Marawi City in the Bangsamoro Parliament

blocks.text: BARMM POLLS. Princess Pala Gandamra, the bet of Serbisyong Inklusibo-Alyansang Progresibo Party, is a physician and a former councilor of Marawi City.
SIAP's Facebook Page
Princess Pala Gandamra, the wife of Marawi Vice Mayor Majul Gandamra, is enjoying an overwhelming lead in the race to represent Marawi City in the Bangsamoro Parliament

COTABATO CITY, Philippines – Physician Princess Pala Gandamra, the matriarch of the Gandamra political dynasty, is enjoying an overwhelming lead in the race for the parliamentary seat of Marawi City and the first district of Lanao del Sur in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).
Gandamra has received 55,011 votes so far, according to 92.38% of total election returns as of September 14, 9:59pm. Her closest competitor, Adbulrahman Taher, only has 7,239 votes.
She is the candidate of Serbisyong Inklusibo-Alyansang Progresibo Party (SIAP), which is led by Lanao del Sur Governor Mamintal Adiong Jr.

A former legislator of Marawi’s City Council, Gandamra is known as the mother of Marawi Mayor Shariff Gandamra and Councilor Mohammad Shaquille Gandamra, and the wife of former Marawi mayor and incumbent Marawi Vice Mayor Majul Gandamra.

The SIAP, together with the Bangsamoro Peoples Party and Al-Ittihad-Ungaya sa Kawagib Nu Bangsamoro, form the BARMM Grand Coalition, a regional political party headed by Abdulrahman Rubbil Sangki Mangudadatu. – Rappler.com

articles.title: BFP, UBJP get more than 500,000 votes each in latest PPCRV count
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Two regional parliament political parties have so far obtained more than 500,000 votes, based on the latest unofficial parallel count by the Parish Pastoral Council for…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Two regional parliament political parties have so far obtained more than 500,000 votes, based on the latest unofficial parallel count by the Parish Pastoral Council for Responsible Voting (PPCRV).
As of 9:43 p.m. on Monday, Sept. 14, the Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP) already had 602,852 votes, while the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP) obtained 557,070 votes.

The BARMM Grand Coalition received 360,278 votes, based on the initial count, less than two hours after the conclusion of the first-ever parliamentary elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).

As the Bangsamoro Transition Authority explained, for the regional parliamentary political party (RPPP), voters will choose a party rather than an individual candidate, and that the 40 allocated seats will be distributed based on each party’s share of the vote, with the party’s nominees filling the seats it wins.

The Commission on Elections said only the RPPPs that obtained at least two and a half percent, or 2.5%, of the total votes cast, or valid votes, for all RPPPs are qualified to participate in the allocation of the seats.

articles.title: Man killed by police after woman, baby reportedly shot in west Edmonton home
articles.summary: Alberta's police watchdog is investigating after Edmonton police officers shot and killed a man armed with a firearm, following reports the man shot a woman and an infant at a home in west Edmonton…

image.caption: Alberta's police watchdog is investigating a fatal police shooting in west Edmonton on Sunday. (Manuel Carrillos Avalos/Radio-Canada)

blocks.text: Edmonton

Alberta's police watchdog is investigating after Edmonton police officers shot and killed a man armed with a firearm, following reports the man shot a woman and an infant at a home in west Edmonton Sunday.
Alberta's police watchdog is investigating the incident
Edmonton Police Service said in a news release Sunday night that the man, 36, died at the scene.

EPS said that officers responded to a residence in the area of Donsdale Drive and 45th Avenue Sunday morning where it was reported that a man with a firearm entered the home and shot a woman and infant inside.
According to police, when officers arrived at the scene they were "met by witnesses and the injured parties and immediately began establishing containment of the residence."
The 36-year-old man then opened the front door armed with a gun and when he did not comply with verbal direction, three officers discharged their firearms, EPS said.
The EPS tactical emergency medical support team attempted life-saving measures, but the man died at the scene, police said.
An infant and two women were treated and transported to hospital by EMS with non-life-threatening injuries. No police officers were injured.
The Police Review Commission was notified about the incident and has since directed the the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) to investigate.

articles.title: CBS’s 60 Minutes accused of peddling pro-Iran war propaganda in segment
articles.summary:
Critics say segment on US rescue operation in Iran was made to boost public perception of Trump’s unpopular war

A US airman has spoken of climbing a 7,000ft ridge with a broken back, arm and…

blocks.text: A US airman has spoken of climbing a 7,000ft ridge with a broken back, arm and shoulder after he was shot down in Iran – and of being rescued by a team of American special forces as hostile locals closed in on him.

The air force colonel, identified only by his codename Bravo, appeared on camera Sunday night on CBS’s 60 Minutes in a segment some critics have labelled Pentagon propaganda to boost public perception of Donald Trump’s unpopular war.

Pete Hegseth, the president’s defense secretary; Dan Caine, chair of the joint chiefs of staff; and Brad Cooper, head of US Central Command; all appeared on the show to talk about the rescue operation. “Alpha”, the co-pilot of the downed F-15 fighter jet, declined to take part, despite reported pressure from the Trump administration to do so.

The airmen were recovered in April in an operation involving thousands of military personnel, including the elite Army Delta Force, Navy Seal Team Six, and a CIA decoy operation to distract and deceive Iranians chasing a bounty for their capture, the 60 Minutes segment said.

Bravo, who was reportedly also initially hesitant to take part, told interviewer Norah O’Donnell that his aircraft was struck by an Iranian shoulder-fired missile – and he realized his parachute was damaged after he and his co-pilot ejected.

“When I looked up and saw no parachute, that was the most terrifying thing I’ve ever seen,” the weapons system operator said. “So I paused, right then. And I prayed: ‘Lord, your will be done. But if I’m getting through this, I need help.’”
Bravo said he was unable to fully untangle his chute and hit the ground hard.
“Based on my description and the injuries that I had, the professionals think I hit the ground, going somewhere between 70 and 100 mph,” he said.
In addition to the broken bones, Bravo said he also sustained a sprained ankle in the hard landing, and serious wounds to his head and face.
“I had injuries, but we all train to adapt and overcome the things that we’re faced with,” he said. “I moved as quickly as I could, despite the injuries, away from the place that I landed.”
Bravo said he managed to hike and climb up the 7,000ft ridge with only a pistol, a communication device and a tracking beacon.

Declassified video broadcast by 60 Minutes showed a “risky” daytime raid by US forces to rescue Alpha, who landed about 5 miles away from his colleague. More than 20 helicopters took part in that operation – and the video showed two of them under fire.

“It was a gun fight all the way in and all the way out,” Hegseth told O’Donnell. “But they got Alpha back. And then we began to, immediately, I mean you’re celebrating that Alpha’s back, but you realize the job’s only half done.”
While Alpha was retrieved about six hours after they were shot down, Bravo’s ordeal lasted about 50 hours.

“As soon as I found a spot that I felt provided some concealment, I started working toward communication,” he said. “When I got to the moment where I could review and think about all that I’d gone through, I sent: ‘God is good,’ as a recognition of all that he had brought me through.”
Cooper said a plan to rescue him was accelerated as soon as it was clear he had survived.
“There was a: ‘I’m hurt, I’m moving,’ and there was a ‘God is good’ message that came in there,” he said. “Now we knew he was alive. He’s moving. OK, let’s keep planning.”

US bombers and drones hit Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces nearby, according to CBS, which showed separate video of those attacks. Two large search and rescue planes with special forces troops and small helicopters landed on a makeshift desert airstrip several miles from where Bravo was hiding.
His first glimpse of the US soldiers was, he said, “one of the greatest moments of my life” – and came with about 1,500 Iranian personnel inside a 10-mile radius, Cooper said.
The extraction did not conclude without incident. One rescue plane became lodged in the desert sand, was abandoned and then bombed to avoid it falling into enemy hands.
Cooper said more than 90 Americans were involved on the ground, supported by several hundred more in the air, and up to 5,000 people involved overall.
“What you need to know is we would have sent more to go get the back-seater,” he said.

CNN reported on Saturday that getting the airmen to appear on television was a priority for Hegseth, who was eager to present a success story in Trump’s ongoing war that has killed 18 US troops, wounded more than 800 and sent oil and gasoline prices soaring.

In a statement to CNN, Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell called that story “a complete lie”. He said the decision about whether to participate in the 60 Minutes interview on Sunday “was each pilot’s alone, because it is their story”.

“As CNN notes, one pilot decided to participate and one did not,” Parnell’s statement said. “Additionally, the [Pentagon] took great care to ensure operational security, sources, and methods were protected. To suggest otherwise is to denigrate every member of our military who participated in and supported the interview.”

CNN further reported Bari Weiss, CBS News’s editor-in-chief, who has been criticized for perceived favoritism towards the Trump administration, put pressure on Hegseth for exclusive access to the story.

A backlash to the airing of the segment was reported on Monday by the Daily Beast. One analyst, Zeteo News media commentator Justin Baragona, posted on X that a CBS staffer told him: “Norah [was] absolutely willing to play the part of dimwit reporter used as a propaganda tool.”
